investmentThesis: Terra closed a $507 million construction loan from TYKO Capital in October 2026 for 1250 West Avenue before offering a single residence for sale, an unusual sequence in South Florida where condo lenders typically wait for heavy pre-sales. At about $4.8 million of construction debt per home across 106 residences, the loan prices in ultra-luxury absorption on the West Avenue bayfront. The tower replaces the 15-story, 238-unit Bay Garden Manor on a nearly 2-acre Biscayne Bay site acquired for approximately $120 million in September 2025 (financed then with a $98 million Northwind loan). Michael Stern of JDS exited earlier; Terra leads with RG Development Group, Gianluca Vacchi's GV Development, and LORE Development. Miami Beach granted the 330-foot height under an overlay zoning district in exchange for developer-funded Baywalk work and conversion of the Bikini Hostel site into a public park. Sales are targeted for 2027; pricing and floor plans are not yet public.

description: Crescent Heights has filed plans for a 43-story, approximately 557-foot mixed-use tower at 1575 Alton Road in Miami Beach's Flamingo / Lummus neighborhood, east of West Avenue on the site of a 1935 Firestone building later converted to restaurant use. RSP Architects designed a slender tower rising from a multi-story podium with white and brown-toned facades, floor-to-ceiling glazing, projecting balconies, and a perforated screen concealing structured parking. The Live Local Act filing calls for 163 residences, including 62 workforce units on the lower floors (households up to 120% AMI) and about 101 market-rate residences from roughly the 15th floor through level 43. Floridian Development has described those upper homes as likely for-sale condominiums; the same outlet's project record lists the usage as multifamily, and Crescent Heights has not confirmed a sales program. Filed program elements include about 4,107 square feet of indoor amenity space, a swimming pool, outdoor terraces, resident club areas, 1,739 square feet of Alton Road retail, and 149 parking spaces. The proposal is under administrative review and has not been approved. Pricing, floor plans, and a sales or lease timeline have not been released.
editorialLine: Crescent Heights filed under the Live Local Act, which lets the tower rise past the height Miami Beach zoning allows.

faq.question: What is proposed at 1575 Alton Road in Miami Beach?
faq.answer: Crescent Heights has filed plans for a 43-story, approximately 557-foot mixed-use tower with 163 residences on the east side of Alton Road between 15th Terrace and 16th Street, in the Flamingo / Lummus neighborhood. The filing includes 62 workforce units on the lower floors, about 101 market-rate residences from roughly the 15th floor through level 43, about 1,739 square feet of ground-floor retail, and 149 parking spaces. As of September 2026 it is under administrative review and has not been approved.

faq.question: Will 1575 Alton Road be condos or rentals?
faq.answer: Not confirmed. Floridian Development has described the larger upper-floor residences as likely intended as for-sale condos, while its project profile lists the usage as multifamily. The 62 workforce units on the lower floors carry rents restricted to households earning up to 120% of area median income. Crescent Heights has not confirmed a sales program, pricing, or floor plans.

faq.question: How tall will the 1575 Alton Road tower be?
faq.answer: Trade coverage of the filing calls for 43 stories at approximately 557 feet, two feet below the 559-foot Blue and Green Diamond towers on Collins Avenue, which completed in 2000. At that height it would rank just below the Diamond pair among Miami Beach's tallest buildings.

faq.question: Who is the developer and architect?
faq.answer: The developer is Crescent Heights, filing through the entity ARRP Miami IV, LLC. RSP Architects designed the tower, a slender residential shaft rising from a multi-story podium with a screened parking garage along Alton Road.

faq.question: Why is 1575 Alton Road using the Live Local Act?
faq.answer: Florida's Live Local Act allows projects that include qualifying workforce housing to seek greater height and density through administrative, staff-level approval rather than the City of Miami Beach's traditional public board process. An earlier plan for the same site called for an 18-story, roughly 225-foot tower with 92 residences, 37 of them workforce units.

faq.question: What is on the site now?
faq.answer: The site holds a Firestone tire service building dating to 1935 that has since been converted to restaurant use. Trade coverage notes it is not a protected historic landmark. The filed plans would replace it with the new tower and a small retail frontage on Alton Road.

faq.question: When will pricing and floor plans be released?
faq.answer: No pricing, floor plans, or sales or lease timeline has been announced, and the project still needs approval. Request updates on this page and Zachary Akers of ONE Sotheby's International Realty will send approval status, official renderings, and any program details as they are published.

Crescent Heights filed a Live Local Act application in September 2026 for one of the tallest residential proposals in Miami Beach since the Diamond towers completed in 2000. At roughly 557 feet, the tower would sit two feet below the 559-foot Blue and Green Diamond pair on Collins Avenue, placing it among the city's skyline-defining additions on the Alton Road corridor between Biscayne Bay and the beach.

The filing replaces an earlier 18-story, 92-unit plan with a 163-unit program that includes 62 workforce homes and about 101 market-rate residences above. Trade coverage has floated a for-sale condominium read on the upper stack, but tenure is not confirmed and the project record is still described as multifamily. description: 29 Indian Creek is an intimate collection of fourteen one- and two-bedroom residences and two two-story townhomes at 2901 Indian Creek Drive in Mid-Beach. Designed by Urban Robot (architecture, interiors and landscape from a single studio) for Trinity Southern with JMH Development, the project pairs Art Deco-inspired architecture with a contemporary boutique program: nine-foot ceilings, floor-to-ceiling glass, bone-white lacquered kitchens with fully integrated Miele appliances, and spa-caliber baths finished in Hansgrohe matte copper and limestone. Amenities include a rooftop pool deck, a Level 3 wellness suite with infrared sauna and cold plunge, 24/7 attended lobby concierge, valet with EV charging, and select-owner membership to The Beach Club at The Miami Beach EDITION.

investmentIntelligence.thesis: 29 Indian Creek is one of the smallest-scale new-construction offerings currently under construction on Miami Beach, which is the strategic distinction. Buyers who have rejected the 200-unit tower experience but still want new construction with hotel-grade service are increasingly looking for under-twenty-unit buildings, and the inventory is genuinely scarce. The EDITION Beach Club tie-in is the most valuable single element in the amenity package: it converts a non-oceanfront address into a de facto oceanfront lifestyle at a fraction of the cost of a true ocean-side residence. Entry pricing of $1.55M and a blended $1,977 per square foot across the three available types place the building in the accessible-luxury band for Miami Beach, a range where boutique inventory at this finish level is hard to find.

description: Miami's first Nobu-branded residences. 75-story Foster + Partners tower on Biscayne Bay, 306 homes from $2.2M, with a $25M longevity program and residents-only Nobu dining.

faq.question: What are 619 Brickell prices and floor plans?
faq.answer: Nine residence types across 306 homes, from about $2.23M (1 bedroom) through $16.5M Sky Villas; penthouses on request. Homes run 1–5 bedrooms and roughly 1,160–5,526 SF. A 4,826 SF Sky Villa (Unit 28D) sold for $20.5M in June 2026 ($4,247/SF). See current floor plans for live availability.

faq.question: What is the deposit structure?
faq.answer: 40% across pre-construction (10% at contract, 5% at 90 days, 15% at groundbreaking, 10% at top-off). 60% balance at closing.

faq.question: When is estimated completion?
faq.answer: Estimated completion is 2030 per the developer.

faq.question: How is this different from the existing Nobu Hotel + Residences in Miami?
faq.answer: Separate product. 619 Brickell is Nobu Hospitality's first branded residential tower in Miami: Foster + Partners, pre-construction on Biscayne Bay, with a $25M longevity program and residents-only Nobu dining. It is not the earlier delivered Nobu hotel residence inventory.

faq.question: Are residences furnished/turnkey at delivery?
faq.answer: Yes. All 306 residences deliver fully furnished and turnkey with Nobu Hospitality.

faq.question: Who is the developer and architect?
faq.answer: Developed by 13th Floor Investments + Key International. Foster + Partners is design architect; Sieger Suarez is architect of record. Interiors by Design Agency · Studio Munge.

name: 619 Brickell (Nobu Residences)
residenceContent: Foster + Partners shaped this 75-story Brickell bayfront tower as five twisting cassettes, rotating each tier so residences open to Biscayne Bay. The site sits on one of the corridor's last walkable direct-bay parcels. Inside, one- to five-bedroom plans, Sky Villas, and penthouses deliver turnkey: floor-to-ceiling glazing, wraparound terraces, custom kitchens with integrated appliances, and spa-inspired bathrooms in stone and warm wood, furnished and styled with Nobu Hospitality.

amenitiesDescription: Based on September 2026 coverage of the revised plans, communal amenities sit largely on the seventh floor and include multiple swimming pools, outdoor seating, and terraces, with about 5,909 square feet of indoor amenity space. A private club on the 36th floor adds about 4,619 square feet indoors with a bar and seating, plus an outdoor pool and terrace. The podium includes 2,556 square feet of ground-floor retail and 156 structured parking spaces. Operator details and the full amenity package have not been released.
description: Crescent Heights, through affiliated entities including 824 Alton Road, LLC and GFO Investments, has revised plans for a 39-story, approximately 525-foot mixed-use tower at 824 Alton Road in Miami Beach, on a surface parking lot along the Alton Road corridor between West Avenue and the beach. RSP Architects designed the building. The Live Local Act revision calls for 149 residences: 72 workforce units averaging about 445 square feet and 77 market-rate residences averaging about 1,368 square feet. Filed program elements include a seventh-floor amenity deck with multiple swimming pools, outdoor seating, terraces, and about 5,909 square feet of indoor amenity space; a 36th-floor private club of about 4,619 square feet with an outdoor pool and terrace; 2,556 square feet of ground-floor retail; and a six-level parking podium with 156 spaces. The earlier concept was 31 stories and 120 residences at roughly 400 to 411 feet. Trade coverage through October 2026 still treats the project as a proposal that has not been approved. Pricing, floor plans, and a sales or lease timeline have not been released.
editorialLine: Crescent Heights' other Live Local filing on Alton Road, a block of workforce housing buying the height above it.

faq.question: What is proposed at 824 Alton Road in Miami Beach?
faq.answer: Crescent Heights has revised plans for a 39-story, approximately 525-foot mixed-use tower with 149 residences on a surface parking lot at 824 Alton Road. The Live Local Act program includes 72 workforce units and 77 market-rate residences, about 2,556 square feet of ground-floor retail, a seventh-floor amenity deck with multiple pools, a 36th-floor private club, and 156 parking spaces. As of October 2026 trade coverage, the project has not been approved.

faq.question: Will 824 Alton Road be condos or rentals?
faq.answer: Trade coverage of the late-2026 revision classifies the project as multifamily and refers to market-rate apartments averaging about 1,368 square feet. The 72 workforce units are AMI-capped rentals required by the Live Local Act. Crescent Heights has not announced a branded for-sale condo program, pricing, or floor plans. Request updates on this page if a sales tranche is later announced.

faq.question: How tall will 824 Alton Road be?
faq.answer: Revised plans call for 39 stories at approximately 525 feet, up from the earlier 31-story concept reported around 400 to 411 feet. That height would place it among the taller residential proposals in Miami Beach.

faq.question: Who is the developer and architect?
faq.answer: Trade coverage ties the project to Crescent Heights and affiliated entities including 824 Alton Road, LLC and GFO Investments (Russell Galbut). RSP Architects designed the tower.

faq.question: Why is 824 Alton Road using the Live Local Act?
faq.answer: Florida's Live Local Act lets qualifying projects that include workforce housing pursue greater height and density with relief from certain local zoning limits. At least 40 percent of residences must be workforce housing for households at or below 120 percent of area median income. The earlier concept for this site was 31 stories and 120 residences.

faq.question: What is on the site now?
faq.answer: A surface parking lot. The filed plans would replace it with the tower, ground-floor retail along Alton Road, and structured parking.

faq.question: When will pricing and floor plans be released?
faq.answer: No pricing, floor plans, or lease or sales timeline has been announced, and the project still needs approval. Request updates on this page and Zachary Akers of ONE Sotheby's International Realty will send approval status, official renderings, and any program details as they are published.

investmentThesis:
Crescent Heights' late-2026 revision lifts 824 Alton from a 31-story, 120-unit, roughly 400-foot concept to 39 stories and about 525 feet with 149 residences. At that height it would join the short list of Miami Beach buildings above 500 feet, on a corridor where Live Local Act filings are resetting what can be built between Alton Road and West Avenue.

The program is workforce-heavy by design: 72 of 149 homes are AMI-capped rentals under the Live Local Act, and trade coverage describes the market-rate stack as apartments rather than a branded condominium sales program. That is the point of watching it. If a for-sale tranche is later carved out, or if the tower clears city review and sets a height precedent for neighboring parcels, buyers already following 1575 Alton and the rest of the Crescent Heights Alton pipeline will want the update first. Approval is not guaranteed and no pricing has been published.

Revised plans concentrate communal amenities largely on the seventh floor, with multiple swimming pools, outdoor seating, and terraces, plus about 5,909 square feet of indoor amenity space. Higher in the tower, a private club on the 36th floor adds about 4,619 square feet of indoor space with a bar and seating, opening to an outdoor pool and terrace. The podium includes 2,556 square feet of ground-floor retail and 156 structured parking spaces. Trade coverage of the revision reports workforce residences averaging about 445 square feet and market-rate residences averaging about 1,368 square feet.

Finishes, individual floor plans, and pricing have not been released.

amenitiesDescription:
Aman Residences Miami Beach delivers the brand's full hospitality ecosystem to a sold-out ownership group of just 22 households. The tower features a private oceanfront pool and the renowned Aman Spa, with treatment rooms, wellness programming, and an oceanfront yoga pavilion reserved for residents and their guests. Dining venues serve both the tower and the adjacent Versailles hotel, with priority access to every Aman Miami Beach facility included as standard.

White-glove service includes 24-hour concierge and valet alongside a dedicated residential management team that operates independently from the hotel to protect resident privacy. Owners may opt into Aman's hotel rental program for short-term income, and receive priority access and preferred status across Aman's global portfolio of more than 35 properties worldwide.

investmentThesis: All 22 residences are sold. Aman Miami Beach is the brand's second urban address in the United States after Aman New York, and its first oceanfront residence in the Americas. It is developed by Vladislav Doronin's OKO Group, the team behind Brickell's UNA Residences, in partnership with Aman and Len Blavatnik's Access Industries. The 22 residences presold in 2021 at a blended average near $5,000 per square foot, a Miami Beach record at the time. The adjacent restored Versailles Hotel will host 56 hotel rooms with interiors by Jean-Michel Gathy of Denniston, anchoring hotel-backed services, an optional rental program, and the long-term brand equity of Aman's global portfolio. Suffolk is general contractor. As of August 2026 the residential tower is near topping out with glazing advancing up the lower half, while the 1940 Versailles Hotel stands within the temporary external steel bracing that retains its north, west and south facades — its interior structure was demolished floor by floor and is being rebuilt inside the preserved envelope, over two new basement levels. Residential delivery remains on track for 2027.

residenceContent: 22 private homes in an 18-story tower designed by Pritzker Prize laureate Kengo Kuma, rising directly on the oceanfront sand at 3425 Collins Avenue. Residences range from expansive two-bedroom simplexes to full-floor homes and a small collection of duplex penthouses, spanning 2,500 to over 6,000 square feet. Every home is oriented toward uninterrupted Atlantic views, with oversized terraces, private elevator access, and Kuma's signature angular yet soft minimalism expressed through undulating forms, tactile Japanese-inspired materials, and a seamless interplay between interior space and the ocean beyond. Full-floor residences and duplex penthouses include private pools. Owners have access to Aman Interiors, a bespoke design service offering signature Aman furnishings to maintain aesthetic unity throughout each home.

amenitiesDescription:
Aria Reserve's more than 2 acres of amenities span three distinct levels: Bay Level, SkyLobby Level, and Garden Level.

The Bay Level puts residents directly at the water with a resort pool and waterfront promenade overlooking Biscayne Bay. The SkyLobby Level offers co-working suites, private meeting rooms, and social lounges for the live-work-play lifestyle. The Garden Level — an entire floor devoted to sport, wellness, and family — includes elite fitness facilities, sports courts, children's amenities, and panoramic water views.

24-hour concierge, security, and valet complete the offering.
architectQuote: Scale and intimacy rarely coexist. Aria Reserve resolves that tension by framing the bay so completely that every residence feels like a private waterfront estate.

residenceContent:
Twenty-two homes on a canal at the edge of a golf course in Aventura, two to a floor across eleven residential levels. Kobi Karp drew the building with planted terraces stepping up each elevation and a porte-cochère carried on signature Roman columns under a green ceiling. Every residence occupies half a floor and opens off its own private elevator lobby, with three exposures — water, city and fairway — and a dedicated service entrance behind.

Interiors are curated by FENDI Casa with The One Atelier as interior architect, and the maison's signature arch recurs from the entryway through to the residences. Kitchens are FENDI Casa with European stone counters and a Sub-Zero and Wolf suite — panelled refrigeration, wine storage, induction cooktop and convection oven — and a kosher kitchen plan is drawn as an alternative. Primary suites take a private terrace, a spa bathroom with soaking tub and separate water closet, and an Italian-made FENDI-branded walk-in closet with built-in fixtures. Every home carries a full laundry room, integrated smart home control, and pre-wiring for motorised shades.

Floors five to fifteen hold the East and West Residences at 3,505 and 3,494 square feet of interior space, each with 1,345 square feet of terrace — three bedrooms on the east line, four on the west, four and a half baths either way. Level sixteen is given to two half-floor penthouses, Acqua and Terra, at 3,887 and 3,876 square feet with 1,912 square feet of terrace apiece, eleven-foot ceilings, three assigned parking spaces and a private rooftop with its own pool.

residenceContent:
B Residences is the flagship of Breitling's new branded residence collection and the watchmaker's first for-sale real estate offering. Rising approximately 70 stories in the heart of Brickell, the tower brings more than 300 condominiums to one of the district's last large prime parcels, near Brickell City Centre.

Designed by Arquitectonica, the building pairs floor-to-ceiling glass and bronze-toned framing with a curved podium of landscaped amenity terraces. The collection culminates in penthouses with double-height living areas and private pools. At its center is a 45,000 square foot, two-level B Social Club, alongside rooftop pools, a private fitness center, concierge service, and indoor and outdoor social spaces with city and ocean views.

amenitiesDescription:
Baccarat Residences Miami spans two dedicated amenity levels plus a lushly landscaped riverfront promenade: the elevated 12th-floor resort deck features a dramatic zero-entry heated saline pool, outdoor spa, private cabanas, summer kitchen, and sun terrace, while a separate waterfront deck offers an infinity pool with unobstructed views across the Miami River and bay.

The wellness program includes a Hammam spa with treatment rooms, steam room, sauna, yoga and meditation studio, and a state-of-the-art fitness center. Social amenities include a Grand Salon, Baccarat Spa, Clubroom with billiards, private screening room, wine cellar and tasting room, private dining room with chef's kitchen, children's playroom, business center, and private workspaces. The private marina offers over 300 linear feet of dockage with a resident yacht for on-demand water taxi service, plus a planned 10,000 SF signature waterfront restaurant.

Services include 24-hour concierge, valet, house car, in-residence dining, housekeeping, pet and plant care, personal shopping, and Baccarat Gold Member global privileges. Parking includes 24-hour complimentary valet parking and optional secured, covered self-parking in assigned spaces.

residenceContent: The first development in the United States curated by Baccarat — the legendary French crystal house whose two centuries of precision, artistry, and brilliance now define a residential address. The tower rises where the Miami River meets Biscayne Bay, delivering 324 flow-through tower homes, 8 penthouses, and 28 riverfront flats and duplexes. Interiors by Meyer Davis Studio translate Baccarat's signature language of light and crystal into residential form: custom Baccarat chandeliers illuminate public spaces, while each unit features 10-foot ceilings, floor-to-ceiling glass, wide-plank oak flooring, Italian stone kitchens with Gaggenau appliances, and spa-inspired bathrooms with book-matched marble. The building is managed by Baccarat Hotels & Residences / SH Hotels & Resorts.

amenitiesDescription:
Over 20,000 sq ft of amenity space, curated by Bentley's design team and furnished with Bentley Home collection.

Arrival & Dining

Three-story ocean-view lobby. Proper English by Todd English — a residents-only restaurant concept by the four-time James Beard Award-winning chef, his first private restaurant. Mezzanine Lounge and Whiskey Bar (Bentley matrix grille–inspired). Cigar Lounge.

Entertainment

14-seat private cinema (Bentley motorcar–inspired). Game Room: golf simulators, racing simulators, VR. Kid's Club. Pet Spa.

Wellness

Fitness center with ocean-view outdoor terrace. Men's and women's dressing rooms: steam, sauna, lockers. Full-service spa with couples and individual treatment rooms; in-residence spa on demand.

Pool & Beach

Heated oceanfront pool with spa, cabanas, F&B service. 200 ft of private shoreline with beach attendants, chaises, umbrellas. Oceanfront beauty salon.

Services

24-hour valet, multilingual concierge, restaurant and yacht reservations, lifestyle and health concierge.

investmentThesis: At 716 feet, Bentley Residences is the tallest residential tower on any U.S. beachfront, backed by a $630M construction loan and Florida Green Building Council certification. Construction went vertical in June 2026 and has reached approximately 13 stories as of late July, advancing at roughly one floor every five to six working days. The foundation pour (a 36-hour, 20,000-cubic-yard operation by Coastal Construction) was the largest residential construction pour in Florida and the second-largest in U.S. history. The Dezervator™ vehicle elevator system is a genuine engineering innovation that exists nowhere else in the world, and the brand collaboration is the first ground-up residential project in Bentley's history. Dezer Development controls 200 feet of Sunny Isles Beach oceanfront at 18401 Collins Avenue, with Aventura Mall, Bal Harbour Shops, and both MIA and FLL airports within reach. Completion 2028.

residenceContent:
The world's first Bentley-branded residential building, with no more than four homes per floor. Arrival is via the glass-enclosed Dezervator™ — a patented vehicular elevator system with four robotic car lifts that delivers you and your cars directly to your private sky garage, accommodating three to four vehicles per residence.

ViewsAtlantic & Intracoastal
Ceilings10 ft Smooth-Finish
KitchensMiele full suite
Smart HomeCrestron + Savant

Residences are delivered fully finished with diamond-pattern oolite stone flooring, custom Italian-designed cabinetry, Miele full kitchen suites, primary bathrooms with soaking tubs, custom vanities and private sauna rooms, motorized blackout shades, and private elevator landings. Every home includes dual laundry, two hot water heaters, and a dedicated A/V closet. The cylindrical glass facade maximizes ocean exposure while the Dezervator delivers residents and their vehicles to sky garages with three to four car capacity per residence.

investmentThesis:
This is Bugatti's first residential tower in the United States. Dubai is the marque's inaugural residential project, under another developer. Prosper Group and Belgium's Versluys Group closed the site for $50 million in August 2026, a $650 million stated development, on a parcel carved from the adjacent One Brickell Riverfront holding rather than found on the open market.

Versluys Group, founded in 1908 and led by CEO Bart Versluys with COO Peter De Decker, has spent more than a century on high-end coastal work in Belgium and the Netherlands, including the renovation of La Réserve in Knokke-Heist. This is the firm's U.S. entry, paired with Prosper under CEO Jay Roberts.

Sales are expected in the first half of 2027, with no price schedule published. Registering now is the way to hold a position before public launch.

residenceContent:
Bugatti Residences Miami rises 60 stories on a roughly one-acre Miami River assemblage at 75 SW Miami Avenue Road, with more than 300 feet of river frontage that opens east toward Biscayne Bay and the Downtown skyline. The site sits in Brickell's urban core, near Brickell City Centre, Interstate 95, Brightline, and Miami International.

Brandon Haw Architecture leads the design, drawing on Bugatti's C-line for the tower form. Interiors are by George Yabu and Glenn Pushelberg. Floor plans, finishes, and the full amenity program have not been released.

Bugatti named Rhodium as exclusive global residential operating partner, with a program defined by white-glove butler service.

residenceContent: The first development in the world created in collaboration with B&B Italia, the four-time Compasso d'Oro-winning Italian design house. The undulating tower, its curved balconies drawn from the movement of Biscayne Bay, delivers interiors personally designed by Piero Lissoni. Every home features 10-foot ceilings, two private biometric elevators per unit, floor-to-ceiling glass, European porcelain tile, and terraces averaging 196 square feet. Kitchens are finished with Italian cabinetry, Bosch appliance suites, and quartz countertops; bathrooms with floor-to-ceiling porcelain, frameless glass showers, and rain showerheads. Located in the Arts & Entertainment District, minutes from Wynwood, the Design District, Pérez Art Museum, and Frost Science Museum.

amenitiesDescription: Casa Cipriani brings its private club model to Miami Beach with an amenity depth unmatched on Collins Avenue. The building houses an indoor-outdoor Cipriani restaurant, a garden bar, a jazz club, and a members-only club lounge available to all 23 owners. A resort pool with full poolside food and beverage by Cipriani connects directly to Mid-Beach's Atlantic shoreline. A full-service spa with sauna and treatment rooms, a fitness center, a screening room, and a library round out the program. Services run at hotel standard around the clock: dedicated concierge, in-home Cipriani dining and catering, 24-hour valet, and continuous security.
architectQuote: Casa Cipriani was designed as a seamless interplay of classic proportions and modern sophistication, echoing the elegance of the grand 1930s-era hotels that line Collins Avenue.

investmentIntelligence.thesis: Casa Cipriani represents the convergence of three rare attributes in Miami Beach real estate: an iconic hospitality brand operating under the private club model, an ultra-limited 23-unit residential count, and one of the last remaining oceanfront development sites on Collins Avenue. The project sits at the northern anchor of Billionaires Beach, three blocks from the Faena District, in a corridor that includes Aman, Rosewood, and The Perigon. At an anticipated entry point of $25 million, pricing reflects the extreme scarcity and the value of built-in Cipriani club membership. BH3 Management's April 2026 refinance signals continued lender confidence in the project, but the underlying thesis is the club model: Cipriani residences trade on access to a specific service operation, not square footage.

investmentIntelligenceData.thesis: Casa Cipriani represents the convergence of three rare attributes in Miami Beach real estate: an iconic hospitality brand operating under the private club model, an ultra-limited 23-unit residential count, and one of the last remaining oceanfront development sites on Collins Avenue. The project sits at the northern anchor of Billionaires Beach, three blocks from the Faena District, in a corridor that includes Aman, Rosewood, and The Perigon. At an anticipated entry point of $25 million, pricing reflects the extreme scarcity and the value of built-in Cipriani club membership. BH3 Management's April 2026 refinance signals continued lender confidence in the project, but the underlying thesis is the club model: Cipriani residences trade on access to a specific service operation, not square footage.

investmentThesis:
Casa Cipriani occupies one of the last significant oceanfront development sites on Collins Avenue, at the northern edge of the Faena District on the stretch known as Billionaires Beach. The 19-story tower echoes the proportions and elegance of Miami Beach's Art Deco hotels while delivering a fully modern living experience: soft, curving facade lines and layered terraces that extend the movement of the ocean into the architecture itself. With just 23 residences, density rivals Aman Miami Beach as the most exclusive branded offering on this corridor.

In April 2026, BH3 Management closed a $105 million refinance on the development site, expanding a prior Bank OZK loan: a capital markets signal on the collateral. As of August 2026 the site is fully cleared — the Coral Reef and Patrician hotels were demolished under Florida's Resiliency and Safe Structures Act, the 2024 law that preempts local historic protection for structures deemed non-compliant with current flood codes — with debris load-out finishing and heavy equipment on site ahead of excavation.
name: Casa Cipriani Miami Beach
residenceContent: Each of the 23 residences averages approximately 3,900 square feet and ranges from one to four bedrooms, with direct oceanfront orientation throughout. Ceiling heights reach 10 feet, and floor-to-ceiling sliding glass doors open onto generous private terraces with panoramic Atlantic views. Open kitchens are anchored by custom Italian cabinetry and outfitted with Wolf and Sub-Zero appliances; imported stone runs through counters and finishes. Primary bathrooms feature sculptural standalone bathtubs, glass-enclosed showers, and backlit stone vanities. A unified smart-home system manages climate, lighting, and building security. Select residences offer direct private elevator access.

amenitiesDescription:
Cipriani Residences carries the full weight of the brand's service tradition across every amenity level. The elevated resort deck features two swimming pools, an outdoor spa, private cabanas, and a landscaped sun terrace, all with poolside food and beverage by Cipriani. Private dining rooms are reservable on demand.

A four-level wellness center and lounge overlooks the Brickell skyline, with a spa with sauna and treatment rooms, a fitness center, pickleball court, and golf simulator. Social amenities include a residents' lounge, library, screening room with premium AV, children's playroom, private salon, and a pet-friendly dog park.

Services include a dedicated Director of Residences, Cipriani-trained concierge, 24-hour valet, in-residence spa treatments, personal training, pet grooming, and away-from-home maintenance.

residenceContent: A curved, cascading glass tower with an organic facade and nautical detailing drawn from the Italian Riviera. Residences range from one to five bedrooms plus Canaletto penthouse configurations, with 10-foot ceilings, floor-to-ceiling glass, expansive flow-through terraces, Italian stone flooring, custom millwork, and Sub-Zero and Wolf appliances. In-home dining and 24-hour catering by Cipriani are reserved for residents, the same service standard that runs the family's restaurants worldwide, delivered to your door on demand. The Canaletto Collection occupies the top 18 floors: 74 ultra-luxury homes, including six penthouses, with expanded floor plates, elevated finishes, and a private speakeasy.

amenitiesDescription: Amenities are scaled for 34 owners, not 400: over 15,000 square feet of shared space across indoor and outdoor zones. The rooftop anchors the building with a 50-foot swimming pool, private cabanas, and a 5,200 SF sun deck. Below that, a Technogym fitness center extends to an outdoor wellness area for yoga and stretching with city and bay views. A full spa includes a jacuzzi, sauna, and massage room. Entertaining is handled through an indoor lounge with catering kitchen for private dinners and an outdoor lounge with barbecue and kitchen. Additional spaces include a screening room, children's playroom, and meeting room. The double-height lobby is designed with natural light and lush greenery. Building services run 24/7 with concierge, front desk, valet, and advanced access control throughout.
description: Colette Residences brings a deliberately low-rise, boutique format to South Brickell: 34 homes across five stories at 1880 Brickell Avenue, where Brickell's urban energy meets the residential character of Coconut Grove. Developed by Meta Development and designed by Brazilian studio OSPA, the building is wrapped in wood, concrete, and glass, with private terraces from every residence and rooftop gardens open to the Miami sky. Four collections span ground floor through penthouse: Garden Residences with private yards and outdoor kitchens, Terrace Residences with expanded open-air living, the core Colette Residences on floors two through five, and two crown penthouses measuring nearly 6,000 square feet each with private rooftop pools. In a corridor of supertalls, Colette's five-story silhouette, private elevator access, and 15,000+ square feet of amenities for 34 owners is the counterpoint: intimate scale, serious finishing.
editorialLine: Boutique by design, not default.

For end-users who want Grove-adjacent quiet with Brickell walkability, and investors comfortable with boutique execution, it fills a product gap the corridor rarely offers at this basis.

investmentThesis: Colette occupies a rare niche in South Brickell: boutique low-rise luxury at an entry that sits well below the branded tower competition nearby (St. Regis, Cipriani) while delivering a distinctly different product. The 40/60 deposit structure (10% at contract, 10% at 60 days, 10% at groundbreaking, 10% at top-off, 60% at closing) keeps most capital until delivery. Meta completed the 1870-1880 Brickell Avenue assemblage (about 0.8 acres) and moved from site control into demolition, with vertical construction expected this fall. In a corridor where assemblage opportunities are scarce, that sequence supports Colette as a low-density alternative to 60-story towers.

residenceContent: Residences range from two to four bedrooms, starting at 2,143 square feet for the Terrace Collection and reaching over 6,100 square feet in the penthouses. Every home features floor-to-ceiling impact-resistant glass, ceilings up to 10'6", and private terraces that wrap from living areas through to primary bathrooms. Kitchens are outfitted with custom Italian millwork by Cesar, Miele appliances including a 78-bottle wine cooler, and mineral-based Inalco countertops. Walk-in closets are finished by Lema. Bathrooms feature Graff matte-black fixtures, Victoria & Albert freestanding tubs, and Duravit wall-hung toilets. Porcelanosa large-format mineral flooring runs throughout. Each residence receives password-protected private elevator access via one of four elevators, plus a service elevator. Homes are pre-wired for smart-home integration across lighting, climate, window treatments, and audio. Two to three covered parking spaces per unit, with EV charging in the garage.

amenitiesDescription:
The Mermaid Club is the defining amenity — approximately 150,000 square feet of waterfront, sport, and wellness space with direct Biscayne Bay access. Features include a 20-slip private marina, floating pools, paddleboards, water toys, a historic beach deck designed for yoga and relaxation, and superyacht-caliber waterfront infrastructure that is unprecedented in Miami residential development.

Inland amenities include a roughly 4,200-square-foot fitness center with Booty Builder® equipment, a spa and longevity center with contrast therapy, cold plunges, and infrared saunas, indoor pickleball and multi-sport courts, two Full Swing golf and multi-sport simulator suites, outdoor putting greens, a sports screening room, alfresco bar and lounge, and dining areas with a demonstration kitchen. Residents receive Yacht Club and Beach Club memberships, waterfront and poolside attendants, organic food delivery, and an on-site market.

name: Continuum 12000 Sport & Wellness Residences
residenceContent: The Continuum South Beach legacy extended to North Miami's waterfront, situated on 4.3 acres overlooking Biscayne Bay and Indian Creek, with more than 1.5 acres of submerged land that will become an immersive waterfront experience unlike anything else in Miami. Ian Bruce Eichner acquired the site through a $48.5 million bulk buyout of the former Mariners Bay Condo. One- to three-bedroom residences range from 1,035 to 3,543 SF with 10-foot ceilings, floor-to-ceiling impact glass, private terraces, 48" x 48" travertine porcelain flooring, fully integrated Sub-Zero/Wolf kitchens with a built-in Sub-Zero wine fridge, and spa-inspired bathrooms with oversized rain showers. Interiors by Paul Duesing Design Partners balance coastal warmth with contemporary finishes. Every residence faces the water.

address: 1755 John F Kennedy Causeway, Miami, FL 33141
amenitiesDescription:
Over 60,000 square feet of amenities anchored by a destination waterfront restaurant with indoor/outdoor dining, resident charging privileges, private event catering, and in-residence and poolside dining on weekends. The Continuum Marketplace is restocked daily with wine and snacks. The pool level features a waterfront resort pool with cabana seating overlooking Indian Creek, a garden sunpool, and a bayfront jacuzzi plunge nestled in lush landscaping by Martha Schwartz Partners.

A private yacht club and watersports dock with paddleboards and kayaks connect residents directly to Biscayne Bay. The wellness program includes a state-of-the-art 3,500 SF fitness center, yoga and movement studio, and a full-service spa with cryotherapy chamber, infrared sauna, steam room, and private treatment rooms. Social spaces include a 6,000 SF rooftop sundeck with adult pool, soaking spa, and outdoor bar, a waterfront boardroom with A/V, an executive co-working lounge, and outdoor garden cabanas with WiFi. The Island Walk — a landscaped waterfront promenade — frames the entire bayfront edge. Family amenities include a children's art zone and playroom, outdoor splash pad, arcade and virtual lounge, and an outdoor glamping retreat. Pet amenities include an indoor dog wash and spa, indoor Companions Lounge, and a covered outdoor dog park. Building services include a Tesla house car, 24/7 concierge and valet, secured e-bike storage, and a Resident App for amenity bookings, concierge requests, and package management.
description: Phase One of the Continuum Waterfront District. A 36-story Arquitectonica tower on Biscayne Bay in North Bay Village — 198 residences with wraparound terraces, over 60,000 SF of resort amenities, a waterfront restaurant, private yacht club membership, VIP beach club access, and Dorsia Premium Membership included at contract signing. Delivery Q1 2028.

investmentThesis:
Phase One of the master-planned Continuum Waterfront District — a 4-acre Biscayne Bay assemblage acquired for approximately $108.5 million between 2023 and 2024, approved under a North Bay Village special area plan in 2025. In May 2026, Continuum Company and Aksoy Holdings closed a $350 million S3 Capital financing package: $261 million in construction financing for this tower and $83 million in predevelopment financing for Phase Two (Continuum Club & Residences East at 1819 JFK Causeway) — a separate ~300-unit condominium with a 96-room hotel and 114 furnished hotel residences targeted for 2030. KAST Construction is the general contractor.

The first luxury branded condo in North Bay Village since its 2020 rezoning, and the second Continuum-branded project following Continuum South Beach — one of the most appreciating residential addresses in Miami. North Bay Village sits at the intersection of only three roadways connecting Miami and Miami Beach, placing residents within 5 minutes of the beach and 15 minutes of the Design District, Bal Harbour Shops, and top-rated private schools. The island is undergoing approximately $2 billion in new investment. At contract signing, buyers receive a Private Yacht Club Membership (fleet of 50'–100' yachts, three half-day excursions included, priority weekend booking), VIP Beach Club Membership with access at Ocean Terrace Beach Club, Collins Park, and South of Fifth, and a Dorsia Premium Membership for priority reservations at the world's most sought-after restaurants across 20+ global markets.
name: Continuum Club & Residences
residenceContent:
Four collections — Bay Lofts, Tower Residences, Sky Residences, and Penthouses — oriented along the curvilinear Arquitectonica facade to maximize sunrise-to-sunset water exposure from every home. Ceiling heights range from 9 to 14 feet, with floor-to-ceiling impact-resistant glass opening to private wraparound terraces overlooking Biscayne Bay, Indian Creek, and the Downtown Miami skyline.

Kitchens feature Sub-Zero and Wolf integrated appliance packages — electric cooktop, wall oven, dishwasher, refrigerator, microwave, and wine fridge in select residences — alongside custom European cabinetry, quartz countertops, and waterfall-edge culinary islands. Primary bathrooms are marble-clad with five-fixture layouts, dual rainfall showerheads, arched double-sink vanities with Dornbracht fittings, and glass-enclosed wet rooms with bay views in select homes. Every residence includes an in-unit laundry room with full-size washer and dryer, double walk-in closets in all primary bedrooms, and wide-plank European wood flooring throughout living areas.

description: Cora Merrick Park is a boutique 74-residence, 13-story condominium at 4241 Aurora Street in Coral Gables, directly adjacent to Shops at Merrick Park. Developed by Constellation Group and The Boschetti Group, with architecture by Arquitectonica and interiors by Urban Robot, Cora is positioned as one of the first WELL-certified residential buildings in Coral Gables — the wellness program is shaped by Spanish wellness brand Lamarca Well, the team behind the Lamarca building in Madrid and its Tracy Anderson Method flagship. The building's exterior blends Coral Gables' Mediterranean architectural heritage — oolite stone, textured stucco, bronze accents, and traditional columns — with floor-to-ceiling glazing and contemporary refinement. Residences range from 1BR to 3BR with den, spanning 678 to 2,651 SF across 12 unique floorplans, with 10-foot ceilings, expansive private balconies, and extended lanais up to 1,118 SF on select floors. Kitchens feature Italian cabinetry, Sub-Zero/Wolf appliances, and stone countertops; primary bathrooms include red light therapy for enhanced wellness. Amenities include the first rooftop padel court in Coral Gables, a rooftop pool with dedicated cabanas, an infrared sauna, hot and cold plunges, steam room, red light therapy, a yoga terrace, state-of-the-art fitness center, resident lounge with catering kitchen, tea lounge, dedicated boardroom, and a 5,000-square-foot ground-level park featuring a Jaume Plensa sculpture installation that connects directly to Shops at Merrick Park.
editorialLine: Wellness meets home in the heart of Coral Gables.

amenitiesDescription:
The amenity program is conceived as a vertical resort by Meyer Davis, layered across the tower's full height. At the base, Cafe Delano is an all-day signature restaurant. The resort-level pool deck features a wraparound pool, cabana lounge areas, and a poolside bar overlooking Biscayne Bay. Higher in the tower, the Delano Members' Club offers cultural and social programming exclusive to residents.

Wellness is anchored by The Source by Delano, a full-floor sanctuary with treatment rooms, sauna, steam rooms, cold plunge, private lockers, a fitness center, and a movement studio. Above 800 feet, the Sky Pool delivers one of the most elevated pool experiences in the Western Hemisphere. At the crown, roughly 850 feet up, Miami's first public observation floor features a cantilevered glass deck and a reimagined Delano Rose Bar. A sky restaurant rounds out the elevated dining program. Core residential services include 24-hour concierge, valet, security, and on-demand housekeeping, pet care, and property maintenance.

investmentThesis: PMG's third supertall nationwide and second in Miami, positioned one block north of their nearly sold-out Waldorf Astoria. The dual-collection ownership structure is the key differentiator: Delano Collection units (floors 20 through 47) are eligible for short-term nightly rentals through the hotel operator, generating hotel-style income, a feature available in only a handful of branded Miami towers. Floors 49 through 75 hold a traditional luxury residential address with select deeded office suites. PMG's track record includes Manhattan's 111 West 57th Street and the sold-out E11EVEN Hotel & Residences. The original Delano Miami Beach is reopening in 2026 under Ennismore, extending the brand's global visibility at residential launch. Ownership includes Accor ALL Live Limitless elite VIP status across the global hotel portfolio. Groundbreaking expected summer 2027; delivery targeted for 2031.
name: Delano Residences Miami
residenceContent: The tower is organized into two distinct residential collections. The Delano Collection (floors 20 through 47) comprises 266 suites, one-, and two-bedroom residences, including lockout layouts. The Delano Residences (floors 49 through 75) offer 155 homes designed for long-term living, with select units including deeded, glass-enclosed private office suites. Interiors by Meyer Davis feature custom Italkraft cabinetry, fully integrated Sub-Zero and Wolf appliances, Waterworks bathroom fixtures, contemporary lighting packages, smart home technology, and fully built-out closets. Floor-to-ceiling glass frames panoramic views of Biscayne Bay, Miami Beach, and the Atlantic from every residence.

amenitiesDescription:
More than 45,000 square feet of indoor and outdoor amenities are operated by EDITION Hotels. Arrival is through a three-story bayfront lobby with 24-hour concierge and valet. The bayfront pool deck is cabana-lined and opens onto secret gardens and 800 linear feet of frontage with direct access to the Miami Baywalk; a second pool and hot tub sit on the roof. The wellness floor holds a full spa, a fitness centre, and yoga and movement studios. Social programming runs through a club lounge, a library, a private dining room, a screening room, a board room, an on-site restaurant, children's and teen rooms, and a dog spa and run. Six guest suites are available to residents' visitors, and parking includes EV charging.

Following the September 2026 completion of the site's condominium buyout, the developer has stated the project moves forward as designed with an added longevity and wellness component and expanded food and beverage programming.
description: EDITION Residences Edgewater is a 55-story, 649-foot glass tower of 185 residences at 2121 N Bayshore Drive, designed by Bernardo Fort-Brescia of Arquitectonica with interiors by Studio Munge. investmentIntelligence.thesis: The case here rests on two things that are hard to reproduce. The first is the land: a 3.5-acre bayfront parcel with 800 linear feet of frontage, assembled at roughly $150 million by buying out an entire 1960s condominium, in a neighbourhood that has essentially run out of undeveloped waterfront. That cost is now fixed and the site is clear to move. The second is the brand: EDITION has run hotels since 2008 but has never built a residence-only building, which means this product has no direct comparable and will set its own pricing precedent rather than inherit one. The published list opens at $3.2M for a 2,315 SF Signature residence, or roughly $1,380 per square foot, which is below where branded bayfront product in the wider Miami market has been clearing. The offsetting consideration is time: vertical construction has not started, so a buyer here is underwriting a 2029-or-later delivery and should read the contract's completion and outside-date language closely before signing.

investmentThesis:
Two Roads assembled this site by buying out a 1960s bayfront condominium (roughly $150 million for the majority of Biscayne 21's units in 2022, with the final eight units bought out for $46.19 million in deeds recorded September 2026), which is how a 3.5-acre, 800-linear-foot parcel on Biscayne Bay came available at all. Very little unbuilt waterfront land remains in Edgewater, and the assemblage cost is now fixed rather than open-ended. The tower is the first of three planned for the site, meaning the first building's buyers own into a masterplan whose later phases price against their delivery, not alongside it.

The brand is the second variable. EDITION operates roughly a dozen hotels globally (London, Tokyo, New York, Madrid, Dubai, Shanghai, Miami Beach) but has never before built a standalone residential product, so there is no comparable EDITION-serviced condominium anywhere to price against. Amenities and resident services are run by EDITION Hotels under Marriott International, which also extends brand privileges across the wider portfolio.

With the settlement fully funded and the litigation that had clouded the site now resolved, Two Roads has signaled it is moving to full execution. “This outcome reflects the strength of our platform and positions us to focus fully on executing our growth pipeline and creating long-term value in the markets we serve. This has been a long and arduous process, and we’re grateful to our team and partners who remained committed throughout. We’re excited to now turn our full attention to realizing the extraordinary potential of this irreplaceable waterfront site,” said Taylor Collins, Co-Founder & Managing Principal of Two Roads Development.

residenceContent: Residences are arranged in three collections: Bayfront on floors 3–7, Signature on 10–40, and Sky on 41–54, with interiors by Studio Munge. Plans run from a 1,919-square-foot one-bedroom-plus-den to a 3,760-square-foot four-bedroom, every one of them delivered through a private foyer reached by semi-private elevator. Ceilings rise from 10 feet in the Bayfront and Signature collections to 14 feet in the Sky residences, behind floor-to-ceiling glass and terraces up to roughly 10 feet deep. Kitchens are custom Italkraft millwork in a European cabinetry program with fully integrated Sub-Zero and Wolf appliances; primary baths are finished in honed natural dolomite with freestanding tubs. Every residence holds a walk-in closet and a dedicated laundry room. Three tri-level penthouses crown the tower with private rooftop pools and gardens.
statusRemark: Two Roads completed its buyout of the site on September 8, 2026, recording a $46.19 million deed for the last eight units and ending four years of litigation. Demolition of the existing structure follows; the developer plans to reopen the sales gallery in Q4 2026.

minPrice.source: The Real Deal, 'Two Roads settles with holdout condo owners' (Aug 31, 2026) and the May 14, 2026 predecessor article, both stating the 55-story, 185-unit tower launched with prices starting at $1.7 million. Per the site's standing rule, priceFrom/minPrice reflect the ORIGINAL LAUNCH price, not the current cheapest available tier — the current developer price list opens at $3.2M (2BR+den, 2,315 SF), which is carried in floorPlans and in the investmentIntelligence stat, not in minPrice.

Re-verify once a groundbreaking date is announced.

units.source: The Real Deal (Aug 31, 2026), Two Roads Development project page, and the developer fact sheet — all agree on 185 residences in a 55-story, 649-ft tower.

stage.source: Traded Miami (Sep 8, 2026), reading the recorded instruments: TRD Biscayne LLC, a Two Roads Development affiliate, paid $46,190,000 for the remaining eight Biscayne 21 units ($5,773,750 per unit), completing the buyout, and increased its Bank OZK mortgage to $151,860,000. amenitiesDescription:
Arrival begins in The Cathedral, an immersive lobby featuring a commissioned mural that establishes the cultural character of the building. The centerpiece is Faena Rose, a 45,000-square-foot cultural and wellness hub suspended between the towers. The club includes an infinity pool with panoramic Miami views, a 40-seat private screening theater, fine-dining restaurant, cocktail bar, cigar lounge, private dining room, billiards room, creative lounge, and content creation studios. At the Sky Bridge's summit, a full-length outdoor pool deck and terrace garden create one of the most extraordinary elevated social spaces in any Miami residential development.

At the podium level, the Tierra Santa Healing House is a world-class wellness destination with a hammam centered on Amazonite stone, longevity clinic, botanical steam rooms, red light therapy, cold plunge, and a full beauty arcade. Fitness programming includes a padel court, golf simulator, outdoor workout terraces, and dedicated pilates studio. Faena's signature cultural programming, with rotating art installations, performances, and curated community events, ensures the building operates as a living cultural institution.

investmentThesis: Over $300 million in contract sales reported as of late 2025, with more than 20% of residences sold before groundbreaking. A $30 million penthouse sale recorded in July 2026 stands as the largest residential transaction ever on the Miami River. In September 2026 Faena published its first penthouse collection, led by a $39.5 million two-story Crown Residence, a collection ask distinct from that recorded sale. This is Faena's first standalone residential project, following the transformative Faena District in Miami Beach (Faena House, Faena Hotel, Faena Forum). A $38 million credit facility from Bank OZK supports the sales and marketing program. Groundbreaking is anticipated in the second half of 2026, with completion targeted around 2030. The broader site plan envisions a phased, three-block cultural district with a private park, wellness center, marina, and public art installations along the river. Landscape by Sasaki. With over $25 billion of nearby investment reshaping the Miami River corridor and roughly 10,000 residential units in the pipeline, the project is positioned at the center of Downtown Miami's most significant waterfront transformation.
name: Faena Residences Miami
residenceContent: The two towers sit on 327 feet of Miami River frontage directly across from Brickell City Centre. Viñoly designed them as a pair of offset slab forms that separate as they rise and reconnect through Faena Rose, a three-story Sky Bridge on floors 61 through 64, suspended nearly 700 feet above the city. Interiors by Faena Design Studio with Bryan O'Sullivan Studio bring Faena's signature warmth to a modernist framework: open floor plans with floor-to-ceiling impact glass, 10-foot-deep terraces, travertine flooring, custom Italian cabinetry, natural stone countertops, and Gaggenau appliances throughout. Every residence frames expansive views of the Miami River, Biscayne Bay, and the Downtown skyline. The penthouse collection includes Sky Villas with private terraces and pools, and a two-story Crown Residence at the top of the stack.

signals.title: Arquitectonica + Gabellini Sheppard
signals.body: 226 residences. Only 2 units per floor on premium lines. Private elevator access to every home. New York's Gabellini Sheppard interiors. The floor-plan efficiency and low density create the conditions for extreme scarcity on the resale market.

signals.title: Miami Beach's only residents-only member's club
signals.body: Five Park's members' club is a first for Miami Beach — adding a recurring lifestyle amenity that creates resident stickiness and underpins long-term hold behavior.

investmentIntelligence.thesis: Five Park's investment case rests on one data point: Terra Group's prior two Miami Beach buildings. At Eighty Seven Park and Park Grove, virtually no inventory has ever reached the resale market, even as values doubled. That hold behavior is a direct function of product quality, location, and floor-plan scarcity — and Five Park replicates all three at a larger scale with a more prominent address. The 3-acre park and Daniel Buren bridge are permanent public amenities that will drive foot traffic and lifestyle validation for the neighborhood over decades.

name: Five Park Miami Beach
residenceContent: Miami Beach's tallest residential tower, with a unique elliptical form designed to create unobstructed 360-degree views from every floor — spanning Biscayne Bay, the Atlantic Ocean, and the Miami skyline simultaneously. name: Jean-Georges Miami Tropic Residences
residenceContent: A 48-story Design District tower with residences from floors 9 through 47 and 10 penthouses crowning floor 48. Interiors by Yabu Pushelberg bring warm, textured residential quality — custom millwork, natural stone, and soft organic palettes throughout. Every home features abc kitchens, Jean-Georges' custom kitchen concept designed exclusively for this project, with fully integrated Miele appliances, custom cabinetry, and natural stone countertops. Bathrooms include floor-to-ceiling porcelain, rain showerheads, and backlit vanity mirrors. Ceiling heights, terrace orientations, and floor-to-ceiling glass extend the residential character through the upper-floor and penthouse stack. The building holds Florida Green Building Coalition certification.

amenitiesDescription:

investmentThesis: Lilli is the second phase of OKO Group's multi-phase Biscayne Bay master plan, following the delivered Missoni Baia next door. OKO Group (led by Vladislav Doronin) pairs with Adrian Smith + Gordon Gill Architecture, whose Miami portfolio includes the delivered Una Residences on South Brickell. The collaboration signals architectural-first positioning on one of the last undeveloped bayfront lots in Edgewater. The developer publishes the tower at 636 feet across 53 floors with 117 residences, from one-bedrooms of 1,348 square feet to a 6,849-square-foot penthouse; pricing has been announced from about $1.65 million with delivery timing still to be confirmed. Early-cycle buyers are underwriting scarcity of bay frontage, a boutique unit count relative to height, and the same developer–architect DNA that produced a top-of-market South Brickell delivery.

residenceContent:
Lilli is planned as a 53-story bayfront tower along Biscayne Bay at 717 NE 27th Street in Edgewater: a sinuous glass silhouette with softly rounded balconies and floor-to-ceiling glass oriented toward the bay, Miami Beach, and the downtown skyline. The curvilinear form reads as movement in the skyline: continuous terraces, deep slab edges for shade, and a vertical rhythm that changes with coastal light from dawn through dusk.

Residences are expected to span one-bedroom layouts through expansive penthouses approaching 7,000 square feet, with ceiling heights reaching roughly twelve feet, layered stone and millwork, and chef-caliber appliance suites suited to serious entertaining. Interiors are conceived as calm counterweights to the drama of the glass: tactile materials, disciplined daylight, and private outdoor rooms that behave as extensions of the living space rather than shallow Juliet rails.

Parking is planned on a separate parcel at 527 NE 26th Street rather than in a tower podium, which keeps the bayfront massing slender. At grade, a tall glazed lobby faces the water, and landscaped edges connect residents to the public Baywalk. Delivery timing and final finish packages remain subject to developer release; the narrative here reflects the publicly disclosed design intent for the site.

South Tower residents access an Ocean Pool with five cabanas, a Lagoon Pool with six private villas (kitchenettes, en-suite baths, sun decks), immersive forest walk, rotating art walk, indoor golf simulator, private screening lounge, game room, kids' club, outdoor Dining Pavilion with grill, Tea Pavilion, glass-encased private dining room with chef's kitchen and wine cellar, and a full business suite. North Tower residents add a 19th-level Residents Lounge with chef's kitchen and private dining, plus complete access to Mandarin Oriental's flagship hotel amenities: signature spa with hammam, saunas, vitality and lap pools, wellness lawn, Technogym fitness atelier, three restaurants, and children's splash pad. Total sales surpassed $1.7B before groundbreaking, with the South Tower 80% sold and the North Tower at 25%. residenceContent: Brickell Key is the only entirely water-surrounded site in Miami's urban core, and the architecture by KPF is built around that fact. The 66-story South Tower delivers 228 residences from 2 to 5 bedrooms (2,333–5,800 SF), virtually all corner units, with interiors by Parisian designer Tristan Auer. Residences feature 10-to-12-foot ceilings, floor-to-ceiling glass, dual private elevator access, full-depth terraces, Italian stone flooring, Gaggenau appliances, and integrated smart home systems. The 33-story North Tower adds 70 private residences and 28 Hotel Collection residences with interiors by Laura Gonzalez, sitting alongside Mandarin Oriental's new North American flagship hotel (121 guestrooms).

name: Mercedes-Benz Places
residenceContent:
Two towers rise 67 stories above Brickell, connected by a mid-rise podium that opens to sky on both sides. The silhouette is immediately recognizable from anywhere in the city. Sculpted horizontal fins wrap every floor, catching light and shadow in a rhythm that references the brand without quoting it literally.

Interiors by Woods Bagot move between crisp blacks and whites and warm red oak, with rose gold fixtures running throughout. Up to 10-foot floor-to-ceiling windows open onto 5-foot deep terraces. Kitchens are fitted with a full Miele suite (induction cooktop, convection oven, refrigerator, dishwasher, wine fridge, and speed oven in select residences), set behind tinted etched mirror backsplashes with integrated technology screens. Baths use Duravit throughout, with black or white stone showers, illuminated ledge reveals, and floating walnut vanities.

The amenity program spans over 130,000 square feet. Residents have access to a rooftop pool exclusive to the building, a Silver Arrow Lounge with racing heritage decor, a custom Mercedes-Benz F1 simulator, a recording studio, and a full wellness circuit: saunas, an onsen ritual circuit, Himalayan salt room, aromatherapy room, and steam room. At grade, Field Operations (the firm behind the High Line) has reimagined the nearly 2-acre Southside Park with padel courts, a basketball court, a children's playground, and a direct connection to The Underline.

amenitiesDescription:
Over 40,000 square feet of interior and exterior amenities span the ground level, third floor, and rooftop — designed by RDAI with the same rigor brought to every residence. The 70-foot rooftop pool overlooks the Intracoastal Waterway and South Beach, surrounded by approximately 15,300 square feet of resident-exclusive outdoor space including shaded seating areas, four cabanas, and an outdoor shower deck. A full wellness suite encompasses a fitness center, private training studio, yoga and Pilates room, sauna, steam room, cold plunge, jacuzzi, and dedicated men's and women's spas with locker rooms.

Social spaces include a golf simulator and screening room, lounge and party room, meeting room, children's playroom, entertaining suite, executive lounge, serenity lounge — each with adjacent terraces — plus a catering kitchen, garden and courtyard, and salon suite for à la carte services. Fouquet's brings five distinct dining and bar concepts in-building, including a patisserie, alongside full residential management: owners receive the same bespoke concierge, housekeeping, pantry stocking, chauffeur, and lifestyle programming extended to hotel guests.

investmentThesis: Developed by a partnership of Raycliff Capital, Fort Partners, Miami Design District Associates (Dacra / L Catterton / Brookfield), and Constellation Hotels Holding — four institutions with combined track records spanning global luxury hospitality, design district curation, and high-end residential development. The Design District's position as Miami's premier luxury retail and cultural destination (home to Louis Vuitton, Dior, Chanel, ICA Miami) underpins long-term value. Fouquet's — the legendary Champs-Elysees brasserie — brings a Parisian hospitality brand to its first U.S. address. Sales launched March 2026; estimated completion 2030.

residenceContent: The Design District's first residential development and the only Florida project by 2023 Pritzker Prize laureate Sir David Chipperfield. The tower rises on nearly two acres at 39 NE 39th Street, its colonnade arrival sequence, glass and mineral cladding, and champagne-colored mullions calibrated to Miami's shifting light. Interiors by Parisian studio RDAI bring warmth and precision in equal measure — custom oak and lacquered wood cabinetry, Sub-Zero and Wolf appliances, and floor-to-ceiling hurricane-rated windows throughout. An 85-key Fouquet's hotel connects to the residential tower, providing residents with Paris-standard hospitality services, priority restaurant access, and a seamless blend of private living and hotel amenity. residenceContent:
Midtown Park Residences By Proper is the inaugural tower within Midtown Park, a five-acre mixed-use master plan connecting Midtown Miami to Wynwood, the Design District, and Edgewater. Arquitectonica's 28-story tower delivers 288 Proper-branded residences. Interiors by Meyer Davis Studio carry Proper Hospitality's design language from the 5,000-square-foot art-filled lobby through 40,000 square feet of amenities on the 7th-floor Proper Floor.

Lobby5,000 SF
Proper Floor40,000 SF
Penthouses20-ft living rooms
Beach club10 min to Shelborne

The residences

  • Studios through three-bedrooms on typical floors
  • Private Collection penthouses: four- and five-bedroom homes with double-height 20-foot corner living rooms, rooftop terraces, private gardens, and pools

Finishes

  • Kitchens: Italian cabinetry, imported quartz, Sub-Zero and Wolf appliances, and Hansgrohe faucets
  • Primary baths: Meyer Davis-curated Jade ceramic walls and Hansgrohe brass fixtures

The Proper Floor

  • Heated 60-foot pool anchored by a Hernán Marina sculpture
  • Adult spa pool and pickleball court
  • 3,000-square-foot fitness center with Pilates room
  • Spa with steam room and sauna
  • Virtual golf and screening room
  • Communal vegetable garden designed by Naturalficial
  • East Lounge with chef's kitchen, plus a dedicated event lounge

Owner privileges

  • Proper Culture Concierge program
  • Preferred rates across the Proper Hospitality portfolio
  • Shelborne By Proper Beach Club on South Beach, a 10-minute drive across the causeway

At master-plan buildout

This tower is Phase 1 (288 units). The full Midtown Park district at completion:

All phases924 units
Office60,000 SF
Retail100,000+ SF
Racquet clubULTRA Padel

signals.body: NoMad Hotels (Major Food Group) operates in NYC, LA, London, and Las Vegas. Their design ethos — art, culture, gastronomy — maps precisely onto Wynwood's identity. This is the right brand for this neighborhood in a way that a traditional hotel brand is not.

signals.title: Wynwood — Miami's fastest-appreciating arts district
signals.body: Wynwood has transformed from a warehouse district into Miami's most visited arts destination. Goldman Properties, Related, and institutional capital have all entered the market. NoMad Residences is the first major branded residential tower in the neighborhood.

signals.title: Top short-term rental yield in Miami
signals.body: Wynwood's Art Basel adjacency, street art culture, and restaurant/nightlife density create consistently high short-term rental demand. Miami's broader STR market has a Wynwood occupancy premium vs. comparable neighborhoods.

investmentIntelligence.thesis: NoMad Wynwood is the arts-district investment thesis: buy the neighborhood's first institutional-quality branded anchor, before the corridor completes its gentrification cycle. NYC's Meatpacking District, LA's Arts District, and London's Shoreditch all followed the same path — the first branded hospitality/residential anchor always captures the most appreciation. Wynwood is 3–5 years into that cycle. At $1,200+/sqft with 6–9% gross yield potential and NoMad's design credibility, the risk/return profile is asymmetric.

Of 329 residences, only 9 remain — penthouses and upper-floor units ranging from $670,900 to $1.5M. The fully furnished turnkey product combined with Wynwood's nightly rental demand makes this one of the most compelling income-generating branded residences in the Miami pipeline, and the brand's first residential extension means early-buyer pricing relative to where NoMad will reset on its next project. For buyers seeking yield-bearing branded inventory in a creative-district address, the closing window represents one of the last opportunities to acquire at developer pricing.

amenitiesDescription:
Spa and wellness: A ground-floor spa with steam room, sauna, hot tub, salon, and massage treatment room, opening onto a terrace and a pool set into the planting. One level up, a fitness studio with a private training room, lounge, and locker rooms sits next to a vitality pool on the landscaped deck.

Rooftop: A pool deck open on every side, with a sundeck and lounge area. An event space with a cocktail room and outdoor lounge is reservable for private gatherings.

investmentThesis:
Surfside holds new construction to low-rise, low-density zoning, the same constraint that makes the Four Seasons Surf Club campus and Arte Surfside effectively unrepeatable. Ocean House is one of very few ground-up condominiums entitled inside that envelope. Scarcity here is a function of the code, not of marketing.

This is Multiplan's third boutique condominium in the Miami Beach corridor, following 57 Ocean and Ocean Park South Beach. Chief executive Marcelo Kingston runs the Miami arm. Arquitectonica has been building in the city since 1977, and Fort-Brescia took this commission directly.

The buyer this building is aimed at wants oceanfront square footage and a short owner roster without a hotel operator on the deed. There is no flag and no resort levy. What is here is scaled to twenty-five owners, not to a sales brochure.

residenceContent:
Twelve stories of transparent glass on a beachfront parcel where Collins Avenue meets 93rd Street. Bernardo Fort-Brescia drew the building as a set of curves rather than a stack of floor plates. Wraparound balconies do the structural talking: clear glass railings, up to twelve feet deep, with wood-like ceiling accents that carry the eye out over the sand. Arrival is under a covered porte-cochere and through a double-height lobby of wood and stone. A walkway runs from the dune line through a landscaped garden into an outdoor lounge finished in natural stone, and every home is reached by a private keyed elevator opening into its own vestibule.

Homes run from two bedrooms to five, plus a two-level penthouse on the top floor with its own oceanfront rooftop. Ceilings hold at roughly ten feet through the building and reach twelve in the penthouse. Floor-to-ceiling impact glass slides open onto the terraces, so the living space reads continuously from the interior stone flooring out to the balcony. Views run east to the Atlantic, south down the beach toward Miami Beach, and west across Biscayne Bay to the Downtown skyline.

Interiors are by Carla Guilhem, whose practice splits between yachts and private homes. The material palette is deliberately short: wood, natural stone, and little else. Kitchens pair custom European cabinetry with Gaggenau appliances and a Silestone island with a waterfall edge. Bathrooms carry double vanities, glass-enclosed rainfall showers, freestanding tubs, and stone floors. The penthouse steps up the specification with Poliform cabinetry and Fantini fixtures, and adds a cinema, a game room, staff quarters with a service kitchen, an ensuite spa with private steam and sauna, and a six-car garage.

signals.title: North Beach — Miami Beach's most active revitalization corridor
signals.body: The City of Miami Beach has invested significantly in the North Beach Town Center and oceanfront promenade. New food and beverage, art programming, and residential investment are repositioning North Beach from undervalued to emerging luxury — the classic early-cycle setup.

signals.title: Art Deco oceanfront — distinctive design context
signals.body: Ocean Terrace's site faces one of the most intact stretches of Art Deco architecture on Miami Beach's ocean side. The historic context and promenade create a neighborhood texture that brand-new towers in Brickell or Edgewater cannot replicate.

signals.title: Miami Beach oceanfront at Mid-Beach prices from 5 years ago
signals.body: Ocean Terrace opens at the low end of Mid-Beach and Surfside oceanfront pricing ($2,000–$3,500/sqft). For buyers who believe North Beach is undervalued relative to its oceanfront location, this is the asymmetric entry point.

signals.title: No competing oceanfront supply in North Beach pipeline
signals.body: North Beach's strict historic district zoning and height limits make it essentially impossible to build a competing oceanfront tower. Ocean Terrace's supply position is effectively permanent.

investmentIntelligence.thesis: Ocean Terrace is the North Beach conviction bet: a first-mover on Miami Beach's last undervalued oceanfront corridor, at a price point that already reflects its neighborhood status rather than its trajectory. Mid-Beach was once priced at North Beach levels before the Faena, Aman, and Perigon pipeline repositioned it. The same thesis applies here — but earlier in the cycle, with real oceanfront access and genuine Art Deco context.

The 350 feet of continuous Atlantic frontage creates a land position that is essentially irreplaceable. residenceContent: Occupying an entire oceanfront city block in Miami Beach's North Beach enclave, commanding 350 feet of continuous Atlantic frontage across 2.2 acres. Two sculptural glass towers yield 52 boutique residences and 24 fully furnished resort residences — every one facing east with unobstructed ocean views. Interiors by RAMSA and exteriors by Revuelta blend a boutique hotel, private members' club, curated retail, and tropical gardens by Enzo Enea and Raymond Jungles into a self-contained luxury ecosystem. Boutique residences feature 10-foot ceilings, floor-to-ceiling hurricane-rated glass, custom European oak and porcelain flooring, Italian stone kitchens, and smart home systems. Resort residences arrive fully furnished for those seeking a turnkey oceanfront address.
