architectQuote: There is a growing shift toward residences that feel more personal, more intentional, and more connected to their surroundings. Buyers are prioritizing design, scale, and privacy over sheer volume. OPUS responds to that shift.
description: OPUS Coconut Grove is a deliberately small, six-story building at 3137 SW 27th Avenue — 14 residences total: 12 three-bedroom homes across four residential floors, plus two four-bedroom penthouses on the top floors. Architecture by Miami's Kobi Karp with interiors by São Paulo studio João Armentano and landscape by David O. Inc., the building is positioned as an elevated alternative to the Grove's large-scale branded towers: no 200-unit HOA, no elevator banks, no sales gallery theatrics. Interiors feature premium porcelain flooring and countertops, European-designed cabinetry, Miele appliances, natural gas cooktops, and full-height laminated glass windows with ceiling heights up to 3.60 meters (nearly 12 feet). Each residence has a private terrace; residences 2B, 2D, and the penthouses include BBQ-ready infrastructure. Two to three assigned spaces per residence within a fully autonomous Klaus Multiparking system with EV charging capability, plus dedicated storage and individual wine cellars on the mezzanine. The rooftop carries a 4,300-square-foot sundeck with pool, outdoor gourmet kitchen and BBQ, fitness center, and spa with massage room, dry sauna, and steam room. The mezzanine level holds private offices, a conference room, children's playroom, wine cellars, and dedicated storage for each residence. Ground floor features a 24-hour reception and intimate lobby with 12-foot ceilings. Walking distance (under 5 minutes) to CocoWalk, the Grove's Michelin-starred restaurants, Monty's and the bayside yacht clubs, and top-rated schools.
editorialLine: Coconut Grove, at the scale of a house.
excerpt: 14 boutique residences by Kobi Karp and João Armentano in the heart of Coconut Grove. Broke ground April 2026. Rooftop pool and spa, Klaus automated parking, from ~$2.8M. 50%+ sold.

amenitiesDescription:
ORA is built around Bosco — a 40-foot sky park soaring 500 feet above Brickell, with walking paths, a meditation and sculpture garden, a recreational lawn, and live programming: film screenings, yoga, pilates, and music.

The 9th-floor resort pool features loungers, cabanas, and a sun shelf amid lush landscaping. Two full floors are dedicated to fitness and wellness, including an 18,000 SF center, spa, vitality pool, and yoga and pilates studios.

Four Casa Tua dining concepts anchor the building: Terra (24-hour gourmet market and bakery), Uva (enoteca with 500+ wines and Mediterranean cuisine), Fuoco (wood-burning fire restaurant), and Vento (rooftop lounge with jacuzzi pool, private dining, and entertainment stage). Co-working spaces, a clubroom, 24-hour concierge, and 24-hour valet complete the offering.

investmentThesis: Casa Tua has cultivated an intensely loyal following among ultra-high-net-worth clientele for over two decades — ORA is the brand's first residential tower, a natural extension for an established global buyer base that already knows the brand intimately. Fortune International Group brings proven Brickell execution to the project, with delivery targeted for 2029. Short-term rental eligibility is rare at this address: the vast majority of Brickell luxury towers require minimum 6-to-12-month leases, making ORA one of the very few assets in the corridor with hotel-program nightly yield potential. The fully furnished, turnkey delivery model eliminates post-closing friction and accelerates income-ready occupancy for international and seasonal buyers.
name: Ora by Casa Tua
residenceContent: Arquitectonica's 76-story tower at 1210 Brickell Avenue is designed around the Casa Tua philosophy: warm, layered, and personal rather than minimal or corporate. Every one of the 540 residences arrives fully furnished and turnkey by Italian design house m2atelier, from studio to four-bedroom. Interiors feature 10-foot ceilings, floor-to-ceiling glass, generous terraces, European oak flooring, custom Italian kitchens with integrated Miele appliances, and bathrooms with book-matched stone and rain showers. Arrival is through a canopy of tropical plantings and water features, with a ground-floor restaurant and private club for residents.

name: Pagani Residences
residenceContent: The first residential development in the world curated by Pagani, the Italian hypercar manufacturer whose obsession with art, science, and craftsmanship now extends to 70 all-corner waterfront homes. Construction is underway on the 30-story tower, which features a 240-foot private Biscayne Bay boardwalk and marina. Two- to four-bedroom residences range from 2,000 to over 3,300 square feet with 11-foot ceilings, ensuite private elevators, and terraces from 800 to 1,040 square feet. Only four residences per floor. Two duplex penthouses crown the 28th and 29th floors, each up to 12,200 square feet with 13-foot ceilings and private rooftop pools. Every home is delivered fully finished and completely bespoke, with owners working directly with Pagani's atelier to personalize finishes, materials, and color palettes. Each residence includes an exclusive Pagani automotive sculpture and furniture from Pagani Arte. Eight purchasable guest suites and eight Pagani Paddock private garages are available for acquisition.

amenitiesDescription: Over 57,000 square feet of curated amenities spans three levels, anchored by the signature Palm Tree Club venue at ground level with culinary and entertainment programming curated by Palm Tree Crew's artist network. The Palm Tree Beach Club rooftop features a resort-style infinity pool, lounge bar with garden terrace, and a private members lounge. Wellness facilities include a Technogym-equipped fitness center with climbing wall, a movement studio for yoga and Pilates, and a spa with steam, sauna, cold plunge, and private treatment rooms. A double padel court, a golf simulator, juice bar, valet, house cruiser bikes, and 24-hour concierge complete the offering.

amenitiesDescription:
The amenity program is arranged by level rather than stacked on one floor. A private lobby lounge sits at grade, with a sculptural staircase rising to the mezzanine, where a wellness spa holds his-and-hers sanctuaries with steam and sauna rooms, a co-ed hammam, and private treatment suites. A private dining room on the same level serves smaller gatherings. The Zen level pairs a fitness center with an adjoining outdoor garden.

The roof carries the social program: a lap pool, a reflection pool, a cold plunge and Jacuzzi, private cabanas and sun decks, and a rooftop lounge with a staffed bar and terraces looking across the South Gables skyline. Building services include a doorman and hospitality-trained concierge, 24/7 valet and attended lobby, 24-hour security, in-residence mail delivery, laundry and dry cleaning, pet care and dog walking, grocery delivery, and restaurant reservations. Housekeeping, private chefs, and wellness treatments are arranged à la carte through the concierge. Private storage is available for purchase.
description: Ponce Park is a 58-residence, 11-story condominium at 3000 Ponce de Leon Boulevard in Coral Gables, facing the city-owned Ponce Circle Park. Developed by Allen Morris Company with architecture by John Cunningham of Zyscovich and interiors by Meyer Davis, the building carries Coral Gables' Mediterranean Revival vocabulary into a contemporary neoclassical facade. Residences run from two to five bedrooms across roughly 1,900 to more than 6,500 square feet, with private elevators, ceilings of 11 to 12 feet, and 11-foot-deep terraces fitted with summer kitchens. Ground level holds 25,000 square feet of retail anchored by Quintín Ultramarinos, the first United States outpost of the Madrid all-day dining institution. The 1.2-acre project broke ground in December 2025, with 40 percent of the residences pre-sold at that point, and is expected to complete in early 2028.

investmentIntelligence.thesis: Ponce Park is a scarcity play on a submarket that rarely produces large new condominiums. Coral Gables' design review and low-rise character have kept new supply thin for a decade, and the 2024 rezoning that permitted this building took four years and two rejected proposals to secure. What buyers get is a 58-home building averaging well above 2,000 square feet, with a private elevator per residence, in a city where comparable product mostly means resale in older Mediterranean buildings. The ground floor is doing real work: Quintín Ultramarinos is an established Madrid operator rather than a speculative tenant, and the $11 million Ponce Circle Park renovation Allen Morris is helping fund improves the building's own frontage. The $132.5 million Bank OZK loan closing one month after groundbreaking is the strongest available signal that an outside underwriter has tested the numbers.

Fifty-eight homes averaging well over 2,000 square feet is a different product from the compact-unit towers rising in Brickell and Edgewater, and it is aimed at a buyer moving within the Gables rather than into it. residenceContent: A neoclassical facade on Ponce de Leon Boulevard, drawn from the Mediterranean Revival vocabulary that has governed Coral Gables since Merrick laid it out. John Cunningham's elevation reads as stone and shadow rather than glass, with deep arcades at street level opening onto Ponce Circle Park. The residences sit above, each reached by a private elevator that opens into a wood-paneled foyer and a set of double doors. Ceilings run 11 to 12 feet. Floors are European oak, with natural stone through the bathrooms and custom Italian cabinetry in the walk-in closets. Terraces run 11 feet deep, finished in tile rather than exposed concrete and fitted with summer kitchens, so the outdoor room works as an extension of the interior rather than a balcony. Kitchens are Meyer Davis: handcrafted Italian wood cabinetry, Italian stone counters with double waterfall edges, a Sub-Zero and Wolf suite built around a 60-inch refrigerator and integrated wine preservation, and La Cornue 60-inch gas ranges in select residences. Full-height pantries and concealed appliance storage keep the room quiet. Smart-home technology is integrated throughout, and select residences add wine cellars, studies, offices, and libraries.

description: Turnbridge Equities has filed plans for Reserve at One Sunset, a 20-story, approximately 323-foot mixed-use tower at 1920 Alton Road in Miami Beach's Sunset Harbour neighborhood. ODP Architecture designed the building, which rises roughly 13 feet floor to floor above a podium. The Live Local Act filing calls for 35 residences: 21 condominiums in three- to five-bedroom layouts averaging about 4,288 square feet, and 14 workforce rentals in studio and one-bedroom layouts averaging about 510 square feet, restricted to households earning at least 120 percent of area median income. Filed program elements include roughly 4,343 square feet of ground-floor commercial space, a wellness club with multiple padel courts, a resort-style pool, an outdoor hot tub, and 53 podium parking spaces. The site currently holds the buildings occupied by Pura Vida and Anatomy. The proposal is under administrative review and has not been approved. Pricing, floor plans, and a sales timeline have not been released.
editorialLine: Twenty-one for-sale residences above a private wellness and padel club in Sunset Harbour.
investmentThesis:
Sunset Harbour has almost no new condominium supply. The neighborhood is built out at low rise, hemmed by the bay on one side and Alton Road on the other, and its inventory is dominated by older mid-rise stock and converted commercial space. A 21-unit tower at this scale would be the most significant residential addition the neighborhood has seen in years.

The scarcity is compounded by format. Twenty-one is a small enough count that the building would trade as a closely held address rather than a marketed tower, and the average size reported in the filing puts these residences in a bracket where buyers are usually choosing between a waterfront house and a full floor. Very little product in Miami Beach competes on both counts.

What makes it possible is the Live Local Act. By dedicating 40 percent of the unit count to workforce housing, the project pursues height and density through administrative staff review rather than the city's discretionary board process — the same mechanism now reshaping the Alton Road corridor. That pathway is faster, but approval is not guaranteed and nothing has been granted yet. Request updates on this page to be notified when approval status, official renderings, and any program details are published.
name: Reserve at One Sunset
residenceContent:
A proposed 20-story tower at the Alton Road edge of Sunset Harbour, on an assemblage addressed 1920 Alton Road and referred to in the filing as 1 Sunset Drive. ODP Architecture's design sets a slender residential volume above a podium holding the amenity club, ground-floor commercial frontage and structured parking, with floor-to-floor heights of roughly 13 feet.

The residential program is deliberately thin. Twenty-one condominiums occupy the tower in three- to five-bedroom layouts averaging about 4,288 square feet — closer to single-family proportions than to a typical Miami Beach condominium floor. Fourteen workforce rentals in studio and one-bedroom layouts sit lower in the building under the Live Local Act program.

Filed plans show a wellness club of roughly 22,272 square feet with multiple padel courts, a resort-style pool, an outdoor hot tub and lounge terraces, plus about 4,343 square feet of ground-floor commercial space expected to suit café or fast-casual use. Finishes, unit plans and pricing have not been released.

amenitiesDescription:
The amenity program spans over 50,000 square feet across residential-exclusive spaces and shared Ritz-Carlton hotel privileges. A private rooftop pool deck with cabanas, sun loungers, and sweeping Atlantic views anchors the residents-only floor, joined by a screening room with backlit onyx cocktail bar, an entertainment lounge with chef's kitchen and garden-view dining, and a TechnoGym fitness center with personal training rooms.

Residents also enjoy preferred access to The Ritz-Carlton, South Beach hotel amenities: the signature spa (treatments, sauna, steam room, in-residence services), beach club with dedicated oceanfront service, Ritz Kids programming, and culinary experiences by José Andrés including Zaytinya, DiLido Beach Club, Lapidus Bar, and a new café in the restored Sagamore lobby. The building features a private double-height lobby overlooking a sculpture garden, 24-hour concierge and doorman, and valet parking.

description: Thirty residences. One of the last oceanfront sites on Collins Avenue. The Ritz-Carlton Residences, South Beach is a boutique tower rising behind the Sagamore Hotel at the foot of Lincoln Road — where Miami Beach's most iconic retail corridor meets the Atlantic. Designed by Kobi Karp with interiors by Alessandro Munge of Studio Munge, the building draws on the mid-century legacy of Morris Lapidus while delivering a thoroughly modern program: 10-foot ceilings, full-height glass, wraparound terraces, and Gaggenau kitchens finished in Calacatta Extra marble and honey oak millwork. Two duplex penthouses crown the tower with private rooftop pools, outdoor kitchens, and unobstructed ocean panoramas. Culinary programming throughout is by Michelin-starred chef José Andrés, whose Zaytinya and DiLido Beach Club anchor the adjacent Ritz-Carlton hotel. Residents receive preferred access to the hotel's spa, fitness center, beach club, and the newly renovated Sagamore — all managed under the Ritz-Carlton service standard. The developer group — Lionstone, Flag Luxury Group (Dayssi Olarte de Kanavos), and Ben-Josef Group — secured a $61.2 million predevelopment loan in September 2025, and the project has been converting reservations to contracts with a projected sellout north of $450 million. Pricing averages roughly $4,000 per square foot, placing it at the top of the South Beach new-construction market alongside The Perigon and Aman Miami Beach.

investmentIntelligence.thesis: The Ritz-Carlton Residences, South Beach occupies a rare position: a branded, boutique oceanfront tower at the terminus of Lincoln Road with only 30 units. At roughly $4,000/SF, pricing sits at the upper tier of South Beach new construction — comparable to The Perigon and Aman — but the Ritz-Carlton operational package (José Andrés dining, full spa, beach club, concierge) is among the most comprehensive in the submarket. The $61.2M predevelopment loan from Bank Hapoalim signals institutional confidence, and the concurrent $42M+ Lincoln Road revitalization should lift the immediate surroundings materially by delivery. The primary risks are execution timeline (groundbreaking est. Q3 2026, closing est. Q4 2028) and the premium over established resale comps in buildings like Setai and Continuum. For buyers seeking a turnkey branded residence with genuine hotel-grade service on the beach, this is one of the most compelling entries in the current cycle.

name: The Ritz-Carlton Residences, South Beach
residenceContent: Thirty private residences rise fifteen stories above one of the last oceanfront parcels on Collins Avenue, directly behind the Sagamore at the eastern terminus of Lincoln Road. Kobi Karp's architecture channels Miami Beach's Lapidus-era glamour through a contemporary lens — 10-foot ceilings, full-height glass, and terraces that wrap the living spaces. Studio Munge interiors pair Calacatta Extra marble with honey oak millwork and Gaggenau kitchens. Duplex penthouses crown the building with private rooftop pools and outdoor kitchens. Service and amenities bridge to The Ritz-Carlton, South Beach hotel next door, including José Andrés dining, spa, fitness, and beach club access — plus the restored Sagamore as part of the broader campus.

amenitiesDescription:
Rivage Bal Harbour delivers 25,000 SF of resort amenities anchored by a fully serviced private beach club with 200 linear feet of oceanfront and a curated selection of water sports. Two pools frame the tower — the Sunrise Pool with direct Atlantic views and oceanside fitness facilities, and the Sunset Pool on the western edge, a tropical refuge with bar and adjacent pickleball and padel courts.

The Rivage Spa offers sauna, hammam, hot and cold plunge pools, and private treatment rooms, while the fitness pavilion with high-impact training room and yoga studio overlooks the ocean. Social spaces include a signature oceanfront dining room, breakfast bar, cocktail lounge, media room, library, wine vault, Club Room with billiards, private screening room, and both a virtual golf simulator and a virtual reality game simulator.

Resident services are handled by a dedicated butler and estate manager providing personal chef, housekeeping, medical concierge, laundry, shopping, and in-residence dining from the on-site kitchen. A 24-hour security and valet team, house car, mailroom with secure package technology, and on-site general manager complete the offering.

investmentIntelligence.thesis: Rivage delivers an exceptional long-horizon preservation play: an ultra-low-density boutique tower occupying Bal Harbour's absolute final piece of developable coastline. Backed by the institutional powerhouse partnership of Related Group, Two Roads Development, and Rockpoint, the project carries flawless execution credentials. In a submarket where established legacy resales at Oceana and the Surf Club Four Seasons consistently command historic premiums, entering Rivage at pre-construction pricing offers sophisticated capital an irreplaceable tactical position. Bal Harbour remains the most fundamentally bulletproof luxury micro-market in Florida—characterized not by market corrections, but by perpetual asset compression.

amenitiesDescription: Life at The Raleigh extends well beyond the residences. The restored three-acre estate operates as a Rosewood-managed compound blending hotel-caliber service with residential privacy. Four distinct pool experiences include the restored fleur-de-lis pool, a sunrise lap pool, a beachside pool, and a residents-only pool, each with dedicated cabana and food-and-beverage service. The members-only Beach Club, operated by Milan's Langosteria, marks the celebrated restaurant group's first U.S. location and offers beachfront dining, in-residence dining, and cabana service along 220 feet of ocean frontage. Wellness is anchored by a Rosewood Asaya Spa spanning 4,000 square feet and a double-height fitness center. Restored heritage spaces include the Martini Bar and Tiger Room, returned to their original Art Deco grandeur. Dining extends to a signature Rosewood restaurant within the historic South Seas building. Residents receive 24-hour concierge, housekeeping, and access to the full global Rosewood privileges network.
architectQuote: This fresh, historic restoration and renovation of The Raleigh joins a private beach club with a Latin beat and elegant residences of demure black, white and ivory. This mixture is the best Miami cocktail that I can imagine.

description: One of Miami Beach's most significant redevelopments, Rosewood Residences Miami Beach returns the legendary 1940 Raleigh Hotel to its place at the center of South Beach culture. Spanning three oceanfront acres at 1775 Collins Avenue, the project unites the historic Raleigh, Richmond, and South Seas hotels into a single Rosewood-branded compound featuring a restored 60-suite hotel, approximately 52 ultra-luxury residences in a new 17-story tower, and a members-only Beach Club. Interiors and restoration are designed by Peter Marino with Kobi Karp handling the tower architecture. The property includes 220 feet of direct ocean frontage, four swimming pools anchored by the Raleigh's iconic fleur-de-lis pool, and the first U.S. outpost of Milan's Langosteria restaurant. Originally acquired in 2019 by SHVO, the project changed hands in late 2025 when Nahla Capital purchased the development site for $270 million. Nahla, which also developed Rosewood Residences Beverly Hills, has retained the Rosewood brand partnership and is relaunching sales in 2026. Fresh Historic Preservation Board approvals are required before vertical construction resumes.
editorialLine: Where South Beach began. Where it returns.
investmentThesis: The Raleigh anchors the Collins Avenue stretch between 14th and 20th Streets now known as Billionaires' Beach. Nahla Capital's $270 million acquisition in late 2025 reset a project that had stalled under prior ownership; the firm's track record with Rosewood Residences Beverly Hills brings operational credibility to the brand partnership. Nahla's plan presented to the Miami Beach Planning Board in July 2026 calls for about 52 residences alongside the restored 60-suite hotel, well below the 84 residential units entitled in 2020. The competitive set (Shore Club, Aman, Bulgari) confirms the micro-market is being repositioned at the highest tier of global resort-residential development. Full Rosewood hotel services, a Langosteria-operated Beach Club, four pools, and the restoration of one of America's most recognized swimming pools form a hospitality wrapper few South Florida projects can match.
name: Rosewood Residences Miami Beach
residenceContent: Rosewood Residences Miami Beach occupies a new 17-story oceanfront tower set within the restored three-acre Raleigh estate. Layouts range from two to five bedrooms in the main tower, with penthouses offering four to seven bedrooms and up to 13,218 square feet of interior space plus expansive wraparound terraces. Peter Marino's interiors draw on The Raleigh's Art Deco heritage through marble, onyx, decorative plasters, and custom woodwork. Every home features floor-to-ceiling windows, generous outdoor living space, and direct sightlines to the Atlantic. Access is through a private porte-cochere entrance, and residents are served by two dedicated lobbies furnished with art and objects curated by Marino. The composition is intentionally horizontal and estate-like, designed to feel more like a collection of private oceanfront homes than a conventional tower.

Trade reporting (TradedMiami) described Fort Partners closing the final condominium at 9165 Collins Avenue — Surfside's Seaway at The Surf Club North — with aggregate sellout cited above $386 million, a final sale near $41 million, and about $38.6 million average across ten residences ($386 million ÷ 10). With only ten homes in the building, ownership float is minimal; the open question is no longer availability but delivery into Four Seasons–managed operations (early 2026), secondary-market liquidity, and how this inventory trades against the rest of The Surf Club campus.
name: Seaway North at The Surf Club
residenceContent:
Seaway North is an 11-story building of ten ultra-luxury residences on a 1-acre Surfside oceanfront site, designed by Joseph Dirand in the same material language as its record-setting sister tower. Seven full-floor tower residences offer uninterrupted flow-through views from Biscayne Bay to the Atlantic Ocean. A two-story beach villa on the ground floors provides direct-access-to-sand living on The Surf Club campus. The penthouse crowns the 10th floor with panoramic exposures in every direction — with further curated homes completing the ten-residence boutique lineup.

Dirand has carried forward the design vocabulary that defined Seaway South — Perla stone terraces that read as if carved from the beach itself, wood-paneled interiors recalling classic yacht staterooms, champagne-colored window frames, and brass hardware throughout. Dedicated elevator landings for the tower homes. No shared walls between residences. The closest thing to single-family oceanfront living inside a Four Seasons-managed building.
tagline: Ten residences. Fully sold at The Surf Club.

amenitiesDescription:
The pool deck is the center of the building: a resort-style pool with integrated in-pool lounging steps, a landscaped sun shelf with panoramic views, and an outdoor bar and sink for casual gatherings. Wellness runs alongside it, with a fitness center carrying cardio, strength equipment and free weights, a sauna for heat therapy, and an outdoor yoga lawn for open-air practice.

Indoors, the residents' club room and social lounge carries sculptural lighting, an entertainer's kitchen, and generous seating; a co-working center offers dedicated desks and private booths, with an A/V-ready conference room beside it. The ground plane is built for families: a children's playground, a half basketball court with a court wall, a splash fountain set within the garden, and a dog park. Building services include an intimate arrival lobby with 24-hour concierge, a smart package room with integrated lockbox, dedicated resident and bicycle storage, controlled-access entry, on-site property management, a resident app for amenity reservations and valet coordination, and assigned parking with 24-hour valet.

description: Seventeen Gables is a 117-residence, eight-story condominium at 1715 Douglas Road on the eastern edge of Coral Gables. Developed by Ascendra Capital and BAM Property Development, with design and interiors by New York-based Asprea Studio and Caymares Martin A&E Design as architect of record, it is positioned as attainable luxury in a submarket that produces very little new condominium supply and prices almost all of it well above this. Residences run from one to three bedrooms across 557 to 1,428 square feet, with nine-foot ceilings, floor-to-ceiling impact glass, a balcony with every home, engineered stone counters paired with European-style cabinetry, a Bosch cooking suite with paneled Fisher & Paykel refrigeration and dishwasher, spa-inspired baths with floating vanities, and Blomberg washer-dryers in residence. Released pricing as of June 2026 runs from $634,900 for a 557 square foot one-bedroom to $1,893,900 for the 1,428 square foot three-bedroom, with association dues budgeted at $1.60 per square foot. At eight stories it is among the tallest buildings in the East Gables, with panoramic views spanning the Coral Gables tree canopy to the Miami skyline. The amenity program includes a resort-style pool with in-pool lounging steps and a landscaped sun shelf, a fitness center and sauna, an outdoor yoga lawn, a residents' club room with entertainer's kitchen, a co-working center with private booths and an A/V-ready conference room, plus a half basketball court, children's playground, ground-level splash fountain, and dog park, with 24-hour concierge and valet alongside assigned parking. The project closed a $60 million construction loan from Dwight Mortgage Trust in February 2026, broke ground that May, and is expected to deliver in the first quarter of 2028.

faq.question: How much do residences at Seventeen Gables cost?
faq.answer: Released pricing as of June 2026 runs from $634,900 for a 557 SF one-bedroom to $1,893,900 for the 1,428 SF three-bedroom with two and a half baths. One-bedrooms are priced from $634,900 to $798,900, one-bedroom-plus-den plans from $820,900, and two-bedrooms from $861,900 to $1,243,900. Across the released sheet that works out to roughly $955 to $1,377 per square foot, averaging about $1,132. Pricing is subject to change without notice.

faq.question: What is the deposit structure at Seventeen Gables?
faq.answer: Forty percent is due before closing, spread across four payments: 10% at contract, 10% at 90 days from contract, 10% at 180 days from contract, and 10% at top-off, with the balance due at closing. That is a gentler schedule than the 20%-at-contract structures typical of Miami's ultra-luxury tier.

faq.question: When will Seventeen Gables be completed?
faq.answer: Estimated completion is the first quarter of 2028. Dwight Mortgage Trust closed a $60 million construction loan in February 2026 and the developers broke ground in May 2026, concurrent with the sales launch rather than after clearing a pre-sale threshold, so the schedule does not depend on absorption.

faq.question: What are the HOA fees at Seventeen Gables?
faq.answer: Association dues are budgeted at $1.60 per square foot, which works out to roughly $891 a month for a 557 SF one-bedroom and about $2,285 a month for the 1,428 SF three-bedroom. Figures are estimates and subject to change.

faq.question: Where is Seventeen Gables located?
faq.answer: At 1715 Douglas Road, at Alhambra Circle and Douglas Road on the eastern edge of Coral Gables. It is within walking distance of downtown Coral Gables dining and shopping, and minutes from Miracle Mile, the Coconut Grove waterfront, the University of Miami, and Brickell.

faq.question: What amenities does Seventeen Gables offer?
faq.answer: A resort-style pool with in-pool lounging steps and a sun shelf, an outdoor bar, a fitness center with cardio and free weights, a sauna, an outdoor yoga lawn, a residents' club room with entertainer's kitchen, a co-working center with private booths and an A/V-ready conference room, a half basketball court, a children's playground, a splash fountain, and a dog park. Services include 24-hour concierge, assigned parking with 24-hour valet, a smart package room, and on-site property management.

investmentThesis:
Coral Gables produces very little new condominium supply, and nearly all of it is aimed at the buyer already living there and moving down from a house. Ponce Park opens at $3.1 million; Cora Merrick Park at $900,000. Seventeen Gables opens at $634,900, below both, which makes it the entry point into new construction in the city and the natural landing spot for Gables renters, University of Miami faculty and staff, and Brickell and Coconut Grove workers who want the address and the school district without a single-family price. The site is on Douglas Road at the eastern boundary, minutes from Miracle Mile, the Grove waterfront, and the Brickell financial district.

The financing is the strongest signal. Dwight Mortgage Trust closed a $60 million construction loan in February 2026 and the developers broke ground in May, concurrent with the sales launch rather than after clearing a pre-sale threshold. That is unusual in a lending market that has grown selective on Miami condominium construction, and it means delivery is not contingent on absorption. BAM Development, founded by Mayer Berkovits, and Ascendra Capital, with David Steinberg as partner and CIO, are self-funding the balance. At 117 residences the building is small enough to sell through without a long absorption tail, and the 10/10/10/10 deposit schedule spreads the pre-closing commitment further than the 20-percent-at-contract structures typical of the ultra-luxury tier.

name: Seventeen Gables
residenceContent: Seven layouts across 557 to 1,428 square feet, from a one-bedroom to a three-bedroom with two and a half baths, with dens available at most sizes. Ceilings run nine feet, walls are floor-to-ceiling impact glass, and every residence has a balcony. At eight stories on the East Gables edge, that outlook runs over the Coral Gables canopy toward the Miami skyline rather than into a neighboring tower. Kitchens pair premium engineered stone counters with European-style cabinetry and a Bosch cooktop and ovens, with the Fisher & Paykel refrigerator and dishwasher paneled to disappear into the millwork. Baths are spa-inspired, with floating vanities and designer fixtures. A Blomberg washer and dryer is integrated in every home, and smart-home control covers lighting and climate.

amenitiesDescription:
The Shore Club Private Collection delivers the rare combination of boutique residential privacy and full five-star hotel service, curated by Auberge Resorts Collection. Residential amenities include lap, leisure, and private pools set in botanical gardens; a world-class spa and beauty atelier; a private residential gym with personal training suites; a residents' beach club with cabana service; library lounge; children's playroom; and a private dining and meeting suite. Residents also receive a Social Membership to the Shell Bay Club, with access to its Racquet Club, Yacht Club, and restaurants.

Building services cover 24-hour concierge and reception, a dedicated Director of Residences, in-residence butler, housekeeping, dining and catering, spa treatments, valet, laundry, and dry-cleaning. The Auberge food and beverage program adds signature restaurants, poolside dining, a cocktail lounge with grand piano, and a beachside beach club — all steps from your front door.

Auberge Resorts Collection manages the hotel and residential services, extending the standard set at Esperanza, Chileno Bay, and Goldfield to one of South Beach's most storied addresses. The Shore Club site at 19th and Collins has been a cultural landmark since the 1950s, and the development represents one of the largest oceanfront restoration projects on Collins Avenue in a generation. Every purchaser receives a Social Membership to Shell Bay Club with access to its Racquet Club, Yacht Club, and restaurants, extending the ownership package well beyond the residence itself.
name: Shore Club Private Collection
residenceContent: A reborn oceanfront landmark at 1901 Collins Avenue, with architecture and interiors unified under a single Robert A.M. Stern vision. Three distinct residential offerings: The Tower (18 stories, 2- to 6-bedroom homes from approximately 1,900 to over 10,000 SF), the historic Cromwell House (4 residences including duplex homes and a full-floor penthouse), and The Beach House (a singular 4-bedroom oceanfront residence with private garage and over 2,180 SF of outdoor living). Every home enters through a private residential lobby on 20th Street, separating owners from hotel guests. Finishes include wide-plank European oak floors, custom millwork, Gaggenau appliances, and natural stone throughout. The Tower's flow-through layouts capture both Atlantic and city exposures; lower-floor residences open onto landscaped terraces directly above the historic Shore Club gardens.

amenitiesDescription:
Over 70,000 square feet of resort amenities conceived as a private residential club — one of the most extensive programs in South Florida new development.

Lobby & Arrival

Grand double-height porte-cochère arrival. ~10,000 sq ft lobby with Great Hall, Grand Staircase, and oceanfront terrace. Signature five-star restaurant with bar lounge, private dining room, and oceanfront terrace. Business Club with John Jacob Astor boardroom and co-working spaces. Drawing room, library, and breakfast lounge with herb garden.

Ellipse Club — Mezzanine

Private Ellipse Club with cognac room, cards and poker tables, pool and billiards, wine vault, 20'×9' LED lounge, golf simulator, workshop and art room, and private chef's kitchen dining room.

Beach Club

Three oceanfront pools including a lap pool and children's splash area. Beach Bar & Grill with indoor-outdoor seating, beach service, and in-residence dining. Private beach amenities — cabanas, chaise lounges, umbrellas. Dog park and pet spa on-site. Multi-purpose events lawn.

West Pool Deck (6th Floor)

The longest infinity-edge pool in South Florida, flanked by a sunken sitting lounge, dining terrace, Sunset Pool Bar, dry lounges, fire pit, and an expansive artfully landscaped events pavilion with sweeping city and bay views.

Wellness Center

Full oceanfront spa spanning an entire floor — spa concierge, juice and nutrition bar, his-and-hers sauna and steam rooms, outdoor relaxation terrace with plunge pools, individual and couples treatment rooms, vitality pool, beauty salon and barbershop, relaxation lounge, and revitalization spa.

Athletic Club

Oceanfront fitness center with multipurpose training rooms, outdoor fitness terrace, virtual trainer room, spinning room, Pilates room, and yoga room.

Residents Club

Library, bar and lounge, multipurpose events space, VIP conference room, oceanfront terrace dining, and guest suites with housekeeping service.

St. Regis Rituals

Signature St. Regis Butler Service — anticipatory and fully personalized. The Art of Sabrage champagne ceremony. Afternoon Tea Ritual. Sommelier-in-residence.

investmentThesis: The St. Regis Residences Sunny Isles Beach is one of the most capitalized condo projects in Florida history: $532.1 million in construction financing from Bank OZK ($418.3M) and City National Bank of Florida ($113.8M), arranged by Berkadia, with a projected sellout exceeding $3 billion. Fortune International Group (Jade Signature, Ritz-Carlton Sunny Isles) and Château Group (FENDI Château Surfside, Ritz-Carlton Sunny Isles) are among South Florida's most proven ultra-luxury delivery teams, with Coastal Construction as general contractor. In July 2026 the South Tower completed its mat foundation after a three-day continuous pour of about 10,000 cubic yards (July 24–26); vertical construction is expected later this year and the tower remains on schedule for 2028 delivery. The north tower is in active sales, with groundbreaking scheduled for early fourth quarter 2026 and delivery targeted for 2029. At $5.1M+ with pricing from $2,700/SF, the project competes directly against Bentley Residences and Perigon at the top of the Sunny Isles market, with hotel-caliber service infrastructure that pure residential towers cannot replicate. The 4.7-acre oceanfront estate, acquired for $113M in 2014, holds 435 linear feet of beach: the longest ocean frontage of any luxury residential project currently under construction in South Florida.
name: St. Regis Residences Sunny Isles Beach
residenceContent:
Two 62-story towers (170 residences in the south and 150 in the north) rise from a 4.7-acre oceanfront estate at 18801 Collins Avenue, commanding 435 linear feet of Sunny Isles Beach. Arquitectonica's signature elliptical form, inspired by the Earth's orbit around the sun, delivers ever-changing curvature that reads distinctly against the open sky from any vantage point. Interiors by São Paulo–based studio Anastassiadis draw from private yacht design: sleek curvilinear forms, couture-grade craftsmanship, floor-to-ceiling glass, and voluminous ceiling heights that frame unobstructed Atlantic, city, and Intracoastal views in every direction.

ViewsAtlantic, Intracoastal & Skyline
TowersTwo 62-Story / 750 ft Elliptical Towers
Site4.7 Acres · 435 ft of Beach
ServiceSt. Regis Butler Service

Each home delivers expansive layouts in 2- to 5-bedroom configurations, with master suite proportions and curated materials and finishes. The south tower (170 units, launched 2022) is nearly sold out and delivering in 2028. The north tower (150 units) is now selling, with groundbreaking scheduled for early Q4 2026 and delivery targeted for 2029.

amenitiesDescription:
Surf House residents have access to the full Four Seasons Surf Club ecosystem, one of the most comprehensive luxury service platforms in South Florida. On-site services include a Four Seasons Director of Residences, residential concierge, 24-hour emergency repair, doorman and bellman, security patrols, electronic-access elevators and garage, dedicated private arrival and valet entry, exterior window and balcony cleaning, sliding door maintenance, secured floor access, and AC filter service. À la carte Four Seasons services extend to on-demand car service, in-residence spa treatments, grocery provisioning, housekeeping and butler service, wellness programming with personal trainers, and dog grooming.

The campus amenities include the Oceanfront Spa at The Surf Club, a state-of-the-art fitness center, the Lido Restaurant and Champagne Bar, The Surf Club Restaurant by Thomas Keller, historic beach cabanas at The Surf Club Private, a private function room, Four Seasons beach service, a dedicated swimming pool on the Surf House property, two additional swimming pools at The Surf Club, the Kids For All Seasons center, and lush tropical gardens designed by Peter Wirtz. The Surf Club Private membership — available to residents — provides access to the restored 1930s clubhouse, its painted ballroom ceiling, and the storied beach cabana tradition that has defined this stretch of coastline for nearly a century.

investmentThesis:
One of the tightest supply stories in South Florida luxury real estate. Resale prices on The Surf Club campus have set all-time records for Miami-Dade County, including a $44 million penthouse at the original Four Seasons Surf Club towers and an $86 million penthouse at the adjacent Seaway South — the highest-priced condo sale in county history. With 16 of 17 Surf House units already under contract, the building is effectively sold out before completion.

Fort Partners secured a $110.7 million construction loan from Athene/Apollo in late 2024, signaling continued institutional confidence in the address. The Surf Club campus has established a pricing floor well above $4,000 per square foot on resales, with the strongest units exceeding $6,000 PSF. Fort Partners' track record at this address — from the original Four Seasons towers through Seaway and now Surf House — has consistently rewarded early buyers, and after Surf House and Seaway North deliver, no remaining buildable oceanfront exists on this stretch of Collins Avenue. The final residence represents the last new-construction opportunity on the campus.
name: Surf House at The Surf Club
residenceContent:
Surf House is the newest building inside The Surf Club's 1,350-foot beachfront enclave in Surfside, an 11-story tower designed by New York-based French architect Jerome Engelking with softly curved alabaster arches, palm-shaped columns, terrazzo cladding, and vaulted cornices that echo the original 1965 structure. The 17 residences span 2,262 to 7,780 square feet of interior space, each with private elevator access and deep wraparound terraces framed by the building's signature arches. Landscape by Belgian architect Peter Wirtz connects the building to the beach through tropical gardens and a promenade of white sand.

Interiors by Paris-based Italian architect Fabrizio Casiraghi draw from a distinctly European tradition — warm woods, natural stones, woven textures, and soft neutrals — that sets them apart from the glass-and-marble vocabulary of most Miami luxury towers. Residences feature terrazzo flooring, natural stone countertops, custom millwork with glass-paneled closets, and freestanding soaking tubs, finished with the quiet material richness of Casiraghi's hotel work at Sant Ambroeus Milan and Hotel La Ponche in Saint-Tropez.

Three residence types are offered. Sunset residences are 2-bedroom homes with 3,049 total square feet oriented toward Biscayne Bay. Sunrise Residence 4B plans deliver 4-bedroom layouts with 7,305 total square feet across three ocean-facing exposures. The full-floor Sunrise to Sunset residences span the entire building at 10,354 total square feet with 5 bedrooms, a media room, staff quarters, and dual sunrise-to-sunset exposures — among the largest single-floor plans on Miami's oceanfront.

The sole remaining residence is Unit 201, a Sunrise Residence 4B plan with 5,518 square feet of interior space and 1,787 square feet of private terracing. The layout wraps three exposures: a 137-foot Ocean North Terrace, a 63-foot Sunrise Terrace along the Atlantic, and a 57-foot south-facing terrace. The living room measures 28 by 31 feet with direct ocean views, opening to a 30-by-21-foot kitchen and dining area and a separate 20-by-21-foot family room. The primary suite includes an 18-by-15-foot bedroom and a 19-by-8-foot walk-in closet. Three additional bedrooms at 18 by 14 feet each, a private office, powder room, and laundry complete the plan. Offered at $30 million.

inquirySubject: Inquiry: Surf Row Residences - Pricing Request
investmentThesis:
Surfside's oceanfront zoning caps new construction at low-rise, low-density — the same constraint that made The Surf Club campus and Arte Surfside effectively unreplicable. Surf Row is one of the very few new-construction condominiums entitled inside that envelope, and at 24 homes it is a scarcity asset by construction rather than by marketing.

The price basis is the differentiating argument. Surfside's branded oceanfront trades at $3,500–$5,000+ per square foot; Surf Row has been trading between roughly $1,263 and $1,979 per foot. That is a Surfside address, walking distance to Bal Harbour Shops and the beach, at a fraction of the per-foot cost of the towers that established the submarket — with the trade-off being one block off the sand rather than on it.

Execution risk has narrowed. The project broke ground in late 2025 and closed a $30.5 million construction loan from Maxim Capital Group in March 2026, funding vertical construction toward a 2027 delivery. LD&D is both co-developer and interior designer, and has committed roughly $1 million to streetscape improvements along 88th Street. Boris Pena brings three decades of practice as design architect, with Alfonso Jurado Architecture as architect of record.

Absorption is holding at the top of the stack. The building crossed 50 percent sold in August 2026 on a 2,524 SF residence that went under contract at $4,995,000 — $1,979 per square foot, the highest print recorded in the building and roughly 55% above the released one-bedroom basis. With twelve homes left in a 24-unit building and delivery about a year out, the larger plans are clearing first, which is the inverse of how most boutique projects absorb.

name: Surf Row Residences
residenceContent:
Surfside is a low-rise town, and Surf Row is built to that scale rather than against it. Four stories on Collins Avenue at 88th Street, arranged around sweeping arches that rise along the entry facade — a deliberate echo of surf cresting on the shoreline a block east. The curves throughout the building take their geometry from seagull wings; the wood grain running through the exterior and lobby reads as windswept sand. Layered glass facades and skylights filter daylight that shifts through the day while keeping the interiors private from the street.

Twenty-four homes range from 888 to roughly 2,200 interior square feet across one-, two-, and three-bedroom plans, most with a den, and the largest layouts pass 2,500 square feet once terraces are counted. Orientation was the governing constraint: the building's massing and unit placement were set to hold clear view corridors to the ocean, the Miami skyline, and the surrounding tree canopy rather than to maximize count. Chef-inspired kitchens with Dekton counters, full-height backsplashes, Miele appliances, built-in wine refrigeration, and custom cabinetry open into living and dining space; bedroom wings stay separate. Primary bathrooms carry freestanding tubs, rainfall showers, custom vanities with integrated sinks, and a raised wet area in porcelain that reads as wood slats.

Every residence has a private balcony. Select homes add rooftop terraces with elevated wood-composite decking, plunge pools, summer kitchens, and outdoor grills. Owners may specify a complete furnishings package by RH, designed for the building.

investmentThesis:
This is one of the last full-height towers on the Edgewater seawall between the Venetian and Julia Tuttle causeways. Aria Reserve, Villa Miami, and Cove account for most of what remains on the water. residenceContent:
Forty stories stand twenty-five feet back from the Biscayne Bay seawall at 456 NE 29th Street, on a block that ends at the water with a park along one flank and open bay on the other. Wynwood, the Design District, and Downtown are within a walk, close enough to use and far enough that the city reads as a skyline rather than a neighbor.

Plans run from an 868 SF one-bedroom with den to 2,763 SF four-bedroom-plus-den layouts on floors 34 through 40, with two- and three-bedroom plates in between. Stacks take south, north-south-west, or north-south-east exposures. Ceilings hold 9'4" through the tower and open to 11'10" on floor 33 and 11'2" on floor 40. Every residence has floor-to-ceiling impact glass and a fully tiled balcony with glass railings, reached from both the living room and the primary bedroom, running past 40 feet of frontage on the largest plans.

Dieguez Fridman kept the interiors material-led. Large-format ceramic tile runs through the living areas and bedrooms. Kitchens pair Calacatta Gold counters and matching backsplash with Bosch and Thermador appliances, including a black stainless combination oven and an induction cooktop, and wine coolers appear in select homes. Primary bathrooms set double stone vanities against Calacatta Gold wet walls. Laundry is full-size in every plan but the one-bedroom, which takes a stacked pair.

investmentThesis:
Coconut Grove is the tightest luxury supply in Miami-Dade, and not by accident: zoning and tree canopy protections cap what can be approved, so the pipeline is measured in single buildings. The Lincoln, OPUS and Ziggurat together add fewer than ninety homes to the village core. That constraint is the whole investment case here — it is written into the code, not into a brochure.

The $58 million construction loan from SME Capital, arranged by Berkadia and closed in September 2026, retires the financing question on a Q3 2028 delivery. The developers had already put the site on their own balance sheet, acquiring it for $8.56 million in 2023, and were 40 percent pre-sold before the loan funded. LORE Development Group was formed by the Brazilian asset managers Leste Group and Opportunity, and partners here with Miami-based Element Development.

What separates this building from its Grove neighbours is the entry point. Ziggurat opens at $3.5 million across nineteen homes, OPUS at $2.8 million across fourteen, and Vita at Grove Isle at $8.5 million; The Lincoln opens at $1.5 million, with a released band running to $3.1 million. For a buyer who wants a walkable Grove address without moving up into estate pricing, this is one of very few ways in — and at forty-eight homes, the owner roster stays short.

name: The Lincoln Coconut Grove
parking: Valet parking; EV-ready garage; enclosed bicycle room; private storage available for purchase
residenceContent:
Eight stories on a 20,970-square-foot corner where Lincoln Avenue meets SW 27th Avenue, a three-minute walk from the restaurants, shops and marinas at the centre of Coconut Grove. Frank Paredes drew the building as a set of stacked, rounded bays rather than a flat slab, and Cité Arquitetura of Rio de Janeiro consulted on the façade: vertical timber-toned fins wrap the corners, and every balcony carries a planted edge, so the elevation reads as canopy rather than curtain wall. Arrival is under a covered entrance off Lincoln Avenue, into a double-height lobby with a sculptural stair up to the mezzanine.

Forty-eight homes run from one bedroom to four, and every plan in the building carries an in-suite den or office in addition to its bedrooms — the reason the bathroom counts sit high for the bedroom count. Ceilings reach eleven feet. Porcelain floors run throughout with three alternative finishes available, eight-foot doors are hung on concealed hinges, and balconies are glass-railed with power outlets and space to plant. Kitchens are Snaidero, made in Italy, with islands up to ten feet, quartz counters, integrated panelled Miele appliances and a built-in wine fridge; Sub-Zero and Wolf are optional upgrades. Primary bathrooms carry marble counters, floor-to-ceiling glass shower panels, Brizo fixtures and Toto fittings.

The top floor holds six duplex penthouses, from 2,713 to 2,983 square feet of interior space, oriented north-west, west, south-west, north-east, east and south-east. Above them the roof is given over entirely to residents: a forty-foot heated lap pool, an observation deck with covered cabanas, summer kitchens with grills and long tables, an outdoor yoga and meditation area, and lounge seating under pergolas. The building is designed to a green building certification, with an emergency generator, EV-ready parking and 24/7 front desk and night security.

residenceContent:
The Mansions on Fisher Island is a limited collection of ground-up, single-family estates on America's most exclusive private island.

An Unprecedented Acquisition Opportunity

Positioned on America's most exclusive private island, The Mansions on Fisher Island represents a rare offering within Miami's ultra-prime market. This limited collection of ground-up, single-family estates combines the scale and autonomy of traditional residential living with the elite, world-class infrastructure of the Fisher Island Club. Accessible solely by auto-ferry, helicopter, or private yacht, the 216-acre enclave provides absolute security and seclusion for the global elite.

Market Positioning & Constrained Inventory

The ultra-prime sector of Miami-Dade real estate operates distinctly from broader macroeconomic trends, driven by sustained wealth migration and an absolute scarcity of waterfront single-family assets. The Mansions on Fisher Island recently placed three of its six estates under contract prior to completion—reflecting sustained demand for ground-up architectural pedigree on an island where new inventory is structurally limited.

Single-family homes have always been a rarity on the 216-acre island, and the three remaining estates—reaching approximately 18,000 interior square feet, the largest single-family residence ever built on Fisher Island—represent one of the last opportunities to secure new-construction, estate-scale living in one of America's most exclusive private-island enclaves.

Architectural Pedigree & Design

Conceived by Portuondo Perotti Architects and developed by MADAR Group USA in collaboration with ASR Construction, the estates are a study in Mediterranean grandeur and contemporary refinement. Each residence features a Tuscan-inspired facade, soaring ceiling heights, and expansive floor-to-ceiling window systems that optimize natural light. Interior spaces, styled by Ford Interiors, utilize hand-selected stone surfaces from top global quarries, custom European cabinetry, and uncompromised finishes throughout.

Outdoor: beachside pool with sunbeds and cabanas, outdoor spa, intimate gardens and meditation lounge areas overlooking the Atlantic, and direct private access to 200 linear feet of shoreline with full beach service.

Indoor: sprawling conservatory with daily breakfast bar, sunrise lounge with catering kitchen, cocktail lounge and speakeasy, bespoke wine room, double-height lobby with open lounge, state-of-the-art fitness center with ocean views, private spa with sauna and treatment rooms, private salon, screening room, billiards room, and children's playroom.

Services: residential butler, on-site general manager, dedicated lifestyle concierge, home management (cleaning, maintenance, floral, pantry stocking), house car, 24-hour security and valet.

investmentThesis: 92% sold, approaching sellout. Located on Millionaires' Row at 5333 Collins Avenue, on one of the last remaining ocean-to-bay development sites on Miami Beach. The Koolhaas/OMA pedigree is rare in the Miami market — The Perigon is OMA's first oceanfront residential project in the Americas, and one of only a handful of South Florida towers by a Pritzker Prize–winning firm. The two-acre site with 200 feet of private shoreline creates a land position that cannot be replicated on this stretch of Collins Avenue. Topped out March 2026. As of September 2026, major structural work is complete across the Main Tower, Clubhouse, and Pavilion, the tower is enclosed, and interiors are advancing floor by floor toward Spring 2027 delivery.
name: The Perigon Miami Beach
residenceContent: The building sits on a two-acre ocean-to-bay site with nearly 200 linear feet of private Atlantic shoreline. OMA's design — the firm's first oceanfront residential project in the Americas — targets LEED Gold certification and uses an angular, faceted glass form to maximize ocean exposure from every residence. Interiors by London-based Tara Bernerd pair natural stone, cerused oak, and textured plaster with floor-to-ceiling windows and deep terraces. Ten owner guest suites are available for visiting family and friends. ODP Architecture & Design serves as architect of record; Gustafson Porter + Bowman (the firm behind the Eiffel Tower gardens) designed the landscape.

amenitiesDescription:
The Residences at 1428 Brickell delivers over 80,000 SF of amenities dedicated exclusively to its 195 residences: no public access, no outside memberships. The crown of the building is Level 70, an adults-only rooftop pool at 850 feet with a two-story sky atrium lounge, lush planting, and a rooftop bar with poolside service. Level 67 houses The Owners Club: a two-story private club with a wine and spirits lounge with temperature-controlled storage, a private dining room with a limited-edition Vaselli chef's kitchen, and a residents' library lounge. A full wellness level includes multiple pools, a spa, yoga and fitness facilities, and a beauty suite. Level 10 offers Antonio Citterio-designed fully furnished guest suites exclusively for residents' families and guests.

The travertine lobby, appointed with B&B Italia furnishings and Flexform pieces by Citterio, Azucena chairs by Luigi Caccia Dominioni, and a bespoke sculptural chandelier, sets the tone from arrival. Services include a dedicated Residential Director, 24/7 concierge, valet, and porter.

residenceContent: The world's first high-rise residential tower partially powered by solar energy, LEED-certified. The building's sinuous silhouette is defined by a "Solar Backbone": nearly 500 photovoltaic-integrated glass panels along the west facade comprising about 20,000 SF of energy-generating surface. Interiors by ACPV Architects Antonio Citterio Patricia Viel (the firm behind Bulgari Hotels worldwide) feature Italian stone flooring, floor-to-ceiling glass, 10-to-11-foot ceilings, custom Boffi kitchens, Gaggenau appliances, and spa-like bathrooms with natural stone. Tower residences run two to four bedrooms from roughly 1,800 to 4,000 SF, all oriented to Biscayne Bay. The crown is a two-story, 11,052 SF penthouse with five bedrooms, seven bathrooms, and expansive bay terraces. No hotel component, no outside memberships, and separated circulation throughout: a private residential address with controlled access at every level.

amenitiesDescription:
Six Fisher Island delivers over 55,000 SF of bespoke amenities across a private island setting with 650 linear feet of shoreline and gardens by Enea Garden Design. The Bayfront and Sunset pools each have an outdoor spa, sunbeds, and private cabanas, with poolside food and beverage service. The Sanctuary Spa features a sauna, hot and cold plunge pools, multiple treatment rooms, and a world-class salon.

The state-of-the-art fitness center overlooks Biscayne Bay with dedicated spaces for high-impact training, Pilates reformers, and a yoga studio. Dining options include the signature bayfront restaurant helmed by a celebrated chef, the Sunrise Lounge café, a private dining room and Chef's Table with a bespoke wine room, a speakeasy-style cocktail bar, and in-residence dining and catering. STARR Restaurants, led by James Beard Award-winning restaurateur Stephen Starr, will curate the culinary program at Six Fisher Island.

The amenities deck pairs a padel court with an imaginative children's playground, alongside two bayfront lounges, a multisport simulator game room and teen lounge, a boardroom equipped with advanced technology, and luxury guest suites for family and friends. A private dock with houseboat sits on the property; the Fisher Island Club's deep-water marina and luxury yacht harbour accommodate vessels up to 250 feet.

Service runs to a residential butler, a dedicated lifestyle concierge, an on-site general manager, 24-hour security and valet, and a house car and house tender to Miami Beach and the Watson Island Heliport. Every owner receives a complimentary golf cart; three dedicated parking spaces per residence cover two cars plus golf cart storage.

Fisher Island's average household income exceeds $2.2M, the highest of any ZIP code in the country. Palazzo della Luna, the island's last condo delivery in 2019, has seen resales more than double: one unit bought for $10.5M resold for $21.3M in 2022, at $4,811 per square foot. amenitiesDescription:
The Rider programs its amenities around a rock-and-roll, creator-first identity. Arrival is through an art-filled lobby with custom motorcycle displays, vaulted ceilings, and a "Lightning" port-cochere sculpture by Van Alpert, with rock photography licensed from the Morrison Hotel Gallery in Los Angeles and Iconic Images Gallery in London running through the building. Recreation centers on a rooftop resort-style pool and rooftop food-and-beverage space, with the ground-floor Leopard Room as a soundproofed speakeasy and lounge owners and tenants can reserve for private events (a garage level above separates it from the residences).

Wellness lives on the RESET floor, with weights, Technogym and Peloton equipment, The Mirror, a cold plunge garden, infrared saunas, a traditional marble Turkish hammam, and a massage room. The VINYL listening room adds billiards, a theater screen, and DJ turntables, and the building includes private office suites, content-creation corners, a roaming art gallery, a pet spa, valet, electric vehicle charging, a gated bicycle room, and a private garage. Motorcycle and bicycle rentals are available for residents, along with beach club access in the South of Fifth neighborhood of Miami Beach.
description: The Rider Residences is a 12-story boutique condominium at 94 NE 29th Street, where Wynwood, Midtown, the Design District, and Edgewater meet. A joint venture between Ciprés and Rilea Group, with architecture by Deforma Studio and interiors by RADYCA, it holds 152 fully furnished homes from studios to penthouses, priced from $550,000 to $2.4 million, 85 yards from the future Wynwood Brightline station. Backed by a $90M Banco Inbursa construction loan (September 2025), the tower topped off in September 2026 and targets second-half 2027 delivery, with 50% of residences sold to buyers across Europe, South America, California, and New York. Deforma Studio's industrial facade pairs with RADYCA interiors finished with Italkraft cabinetry, Bertazzoni appliances, Cosentino Dekton surfaces, and smart-home technology; Restoration Hardware furnishings are available in select penthouse and lanai residences. About 11,000 square feet of ground-floor retail and rooftop food-and-beverage space anchors the program. Amenities include an art-and-motorcycle lobby, rooftop pool, the Leopard Room speakeasy for private events, RESET wellness with cold plunge and infrared saunas, a marble Turkish hammam, motorcycle and bicycle rentals, and beach club access in South of Fifth. Short-term rentals are allowed, with optional management through The Rider Living; buyers can access crypto-backed mortgages through Milo, with closings facilitated by Propy.
editorialLine: Rock and roll comes home to Wynwood. Furnished, rentable, 85 yards from the train.

investmentThesis:
The Rider is an income-first play on Wynwood's transit future. Fully furnished, short-term-rental-ready residences priced from $550,000 to $2.4 million sit 85 yards from the planned Wynwood Brightline station, in a corridor where homes near existing Miami Brightline stops have been reported to outpace broader-market appreciation since the line opened. A $90M Banco Inbursa construction loan closed in September 2025, and the tower topped off in September 2026 with 50% sold to buyers from Europe, South America, California, and New York. That sequence retires much of the early execution risk: the structure is complete and moving into facade and interiors ahead of second-half 2027 delivery. Optional management through The Rider Living keeps operating friction lower than the market norm for condo-hotel style product.

Rilea Group brings a four-decade Miami track record, including J.P. Morgan's offices at 1450 Brickell, and is building here with Beauchamp Construction as general contractor. The same team is also starting Mohawk at Wynwood on the same block. Risks remain typical of late-stage construction and of a market where short-term-rental rules can change, so buyers should underwrite to conservative annual occupancy rather than peak-season highs, and confirm current pricing and the rental certificate-of-use process before contract.

residenceContent:
The Rider holds 152 fully furnished and finished residences across 12 stories, ranging from studios at 386 square feet through one-, two-, and three-bedroom homes up to 1,612 square feet, plus penthouses. Select layouts incorporate dens and additional half bathrooms. Many plans are designed with lock-out studios, so owners can live in part of a residence and rent the rest, or rent the whole home by the day, week, or month. Kitchens are built with Italkraft cabinetry, Bertazzoni appliances, and Cosentino Dekton surfaces, with smart-home technology throughout. Restoration Hardware furnishings are available in select penthouse and lanai residences.

Every home is delivered turnkey so it can generate income from the first night. The Rider Link app connects owners to home-sharing platforms, schedules property use, and handles maintenance from anywhere, while optional management runs through The Rider Living. Buyers can also access crypto-backed mortgages through Milo, with closings facilitated by Propy.

description: A proposed 38-story oceanfront tower at 425 Ocean Drive in South of Fifth, on the two-acre site of the historic 1937 Savoy Hotel. Plans filed by Allied Partners in June 2026 call for 90 private condominium residences averaging roughly 2,000 square feet, a 76-key hotel, and a ground-floor beach club, with architecture by Arquitectonica. Condominium owners would have a private rooftop pool and amenities separate from hotel guests, along with direct beach access. The original Savoy lobby would be preserved within the new building. The building would include 150 residences in total, 60 of them workforce units on the lower floors, as required under Florida's Live Local Act. The project is currently under administrative review by the City of Miami Beach and has not been approved. Pricing, floor plans, and a sales timeline have not been released.

amenitiesDescription:
THE WELL Coconut Grove delivers two distinct amenity tiers — one exclusively for residents, one shared with THE WELL Club members — anchored by a 40,000 SF rooftop wellness oasis and a 13,000 SF ground-level Wellness Club. The rooftop features two pools, a hot and cold plunge, private cabanas, a Fitness Forest, pickleball court, and an outdoor dining terrace. The Wellness Club includes a state-of-the-art fitness center, a mindful movement studio with aerial yoga and a healing gong wall, a communal bathhouse with steam, sauna, cold plunge, and caldarium, hyperbaric chambers, a crystal cave relaxation lounge, and private treatment rooms.

The resident-exclusive Conservatory — a double-height glass indoor-outdoor space — overlooks the tea garden with a reflection pond and hosts co-working, IV therapy, and a Shiftwave Recovery Chair. Additional programming includes bi-annual health coaching, annual whole-person health assessments, THE WELL Locker (Theragun, infrared blankets, lymph boots, FaceWare Pro), an aperitif bar, and an energy-clearing ceremony for every new residence upon move-in.

investmentIntelligence.thesis: Una Residences is the finished product from the same developer behind Aman Miami Beach — delivered, occupiable, and sitting on the last bayfront site in South Brickell. investmentThesis:
Blocks of this scale are uncommon in Coral Gables. The site took six separate transactions and $15.85 million to assemble in 2022, a unanimous city commission vote to approve, and a Mediterranean Revival density bonus of two extra units per acre. No comparable assemblage is currently in the pipeline. Whatever the market does, the supply at this address is fixed.

The building has already proved its ceiling. Villa 4 closed at $4.8 million in February 2025 — $1,675 per square foot, the highest ever paid for new construction in Coral Gables. Forty-two of the forty-eight homes are sold, the project topped off ahead of schedule in November 2024 at 60% sold, move-ins began in Summer 2025, and the final phase handed over in Spring 2026.

What is left is six residences at Phase 3 pricing: two Villas at $4.5 million, two Townhomes at $3.99 and $4.2 million, and two Lofts at $2.55 and $2.7 million. A buyer here is not underwriting a delivery date, a construction loan or a rendering — the homes are standing, landscaped and occupied by neighbours. That is a materially different risk profile from everything else on this site, and it is priced as finished product rather than as a pre-construction discount.

name: The Village at Coral Gables
residenceContent:
Seventeen lots bounded by Malaga Avenue, Santander Avenue, Segovia Street and Hernando Street, assembled into a single 2.6-acre block and built out as Coral Gables' eighth village. De La Guardia Victoria Architects & Urbanists drew it as a piece of town rather than a building — tree-lined streets, plazas, walkways and fountains between the homes, with glorietas modelled on the 1929 Ibero-American Exposition. Nothing rises above four stories. The whole enclave completes the plan George Merrick set out for the City Beautiful a century ago, which is the point of it.

Forty-eight residences across four collections. Twenty-four Flats of two bedrooms and a study, 1,698 to 1,771 square feet of interior space under ten-foot cove ceilings, each with a covered loggia. Four three-story Lofts at 1,881 square feet, with fourteen-foot cathedral ceilings over the primary bedroom and a private two-car garage. Sixteen three-story Townhomes from 3,147 to 3,246 square feet, with wet bars, walk-in laundries, skylights over the stairs and private elevators from the garage. Four two-story Villas at 2,439 and 2,863 square feet, each with a heated pool, an outdoor kitchen with gas grill and an outdoor shower.

The specification is the same throughout: hurricane-rated CGI windows and doors in a bronze finish, wood-plank front doors, Italian kitchen cabinetry with stone counters and backsplash, Wolf and Sub-Zero appliances, natural stone bathroom floors with Italian double vanities in stained wood, seven- and eight-foot premium wood doors, coral stone on every terrace, smooth painted stucco and brown clay barrel roof tile outside. Air conditioning runs in zones, hot water recirculates, and every home is generator-ready and wired for an electric vehicle charger.
tagline: Forty-eight Spanish-colonial residences on a 2.6-acre block in the heart of Coral Gables — built, landscaped and handed over.

investmentIntelligenceData.thesis: Grove Isle is one of the most distinctive residential addresses in Miami — a gated private island with boat slips, 360° water views, and the kind of calm that no mainland condo can replicate. Vita is the first new construction on the island in 30+ years. CMC Group's finish standards, the island's inherent land scarcity, and the Grove's chronic primary-market demand create a combination that the David Siddons Group summarizes simply: 'I am bullish about this project.'

investmentThesis: Only 10 residences remained at TCO, making this one of the most limited new luxury offerings in Coconut Grove. Available inventory includes several four-bedroom residences ($8.5M to $10.3M) and two duplex penthouses with private rooftop pools at $22 million each. The buyer profile has been largely domestic, including local Miami residents transitioning from single-family homes in surrounding neighborhoods. Ugo Colombo maintained direct involvement throughout the project, overseeing elements from facade engineering to material selection. His Miami portfolio spans Bristol Tower, Santa Maria, Epic Hotel & Residences, Brickell Flatiron, and Onda Residences. CMC Group has since broken ground on Four Seasons Private Residences Coconut Grove, continuing Colombo's focus on the neighborhood. La Sponda, an Italian restaurant by Gioia Hospitality Group (the team behind Daniel's Miami), is opening on the property in 2026.
name: Vita at Grove Isle
residenceContent: The only new luxury condominium delivered in Coconut Grove in 2025, now closing with immediate occupancy available. Three interconnected buildings (Mare, Luce, and Sole) trace the island's shoreline, placing every residence directly on the water with both sunrise and sunset exposures. Homes feature private elevator access with dedicated foyers, open-plan kitchens with fully concealed Miele appliances, and bathrooms finished with Italian cabinetry, European fixtures, and book-matched Venus marble. Ceiling heights reach a minimum of 10 feet, with 13'5"-deep wraparound terraces. Smart home infrastructure is fully integrated: Crestron control for lighting, climate, and audio; Lutron HomeWorks whole-home lighting; multi-zone HVAC; fiber connectivity with up to 10-gigabit capability; and WiFi 6 access points throughout. The collection of 12 two-story penthouses includes private rooftop terraces with swimming pools, summer kitchens, and 11-foot ceilings with expanded outdoor living areas.

investmentThesis: The tower combines 387 private residences with 205 Waldorf Astoria hotel rooms, backed by a $668M construction loan from Bank OZK and Related Fund Management, the largest residential condo construction loan in Florida history. The development partnership includes Greybrook Realty Partners, Mohari Hospitality, and S2 Development, with property management by Hilton Worldwide. General contractor: John Moriarty & Associates. As of August 2026, the superstructure has reached level 85 and work has begun on the ninth and final cube, with a winter top-off advertised on site. At 92% sold, the project enters its final inventory window before Q2 2028 delivery.
name: Waldorf Astoria Residences
residenceContent: Florida's first supertall skyscraper, designed as nine spiraling, offset glass cubes that deliver unobstructed 360-degree views of Downtown Miami, Miami Beach, and the Atlantic Ocean. The architecture stacks the cubes at deliberate offsets so each residence reads as part of a discrete sky-block rather than a uniform tower floor. BAMO-designed interiors feature 10-foot floor-to-ceiling windows, custom Italian cabinetry by Italkraft, Sub-Zero and Wolf appliances, Dornbracht and Duravit fixtures, and Savant smart home technology with a custom Waldorf Astoria app controlling concierge services, lighting, climate, and A/V from your phone.

amenitiesDescription:
At Ziggurat's core is an open-air paseo — a curated street-level experience featuring cuisine by a Michelin-star chef, couture ateliers, an artisanal café, and an international gourmet market. Residents receive exclusive rooftop membership to the Michelin-starred restaurant, plus access to a resort-style rooftop pool with hydrotherapy circuit, chef's grilling stations, private cabanas, and lounge chairs. A state-of-the-art wellness concept, custom-designed private event spaces, and direct views into the newly renovated Kirk Munroe Park complete the offering.

Building services include 24-hour valet, a luxury hospitality-trained concierge, mail and package delivery to each residence, dog walking and pet care, and dry-cleaning — setting a new benchmark for boutique new condo development in Coconut Grove.
architectQuote: We were drawn to Coconut Grove for its irreplaceable character — the canopy, the quiet, the sense that nature is always winning. ZIGGURAT is our response to that. Not a building placed in a landscape, but a building that becomes one.

signals.title: Chad Oppenheim — Grove's most celebrated architect
signals.body: Chad Oppenheim's practice is deeply rooted in Coconut Grove's nature-forward ethos. His work commands the highest per-sqft premiums in the neighborhoods where it appears. Ziggurat is his boldest residential statement — a terraced form that references ancient architecture while sitting inside the Grove's canopy.

At 19 units, it will behave like a private residence with condo services. Oppenheim Architecture ensures this building will be photographed, published, and referenced for decades. Grove boutique luxury at this scale has a near-perfect track record: Mr. C sold out before completion; Grove at Grand Bay and One Park Grove have virtually no resale inventory — owners hold.

investmentThesis: The only mixed-use boutique residential project in Coconut Grove. Above the residences, Ziggurat houses 100,000 SF of boutique office space across five stories and 40,000 SF of ground-floor retail and dining curated as an open-air paseo — a Michelin-starred chef restaurant, couture ateliers, an artisanal café, and an international gourmet market. The office tenancy activates the building day and night and creates a level of street-life sophistication that no other Grove residential project offers. Allen Morris Company is one of the most established Coconut Grove developers, and Oppenheim Architecture's biophilic language carries unusual collector appeal in this market. With only 19 residences and 65% already sold, Ziggurat is one of two sub-20-unit boutique projects under construction in the Grove, alongside OPUS Coconut Grove.
name: Ziggurat Coconut Grove
rentalPolicy: Up to 12 rentals per year; minimum 1-month stays
residenceContent: One of Miami's most intimate new residential developments — a low-rise biophilic sanctuary where architecture dissolves into living landscape. The building's stepped form and cascading greenery draw from the ancient ziggurats, using oolite stone, natural woods, and tropical plantings to create an environment unlike anything else in Miami new construction. Just 19 residences feature ceilings up to 11 feet, European oak floors, travertine stone, custom Italian kitchens with Miele appliances, and 12-foot-deep terraces designed as outdoor living rooms. Layouts span 2-bedrooms to 5-bedroom penthouses, with sky homes including private plunge pools and the penthouse claiming a full rooftop with private pool. The site sits directly across from Kirk Munroe Park, currently undergoing a $6.3M renovation.
